stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a reason for building the dam in the beginning?

options.A: To promote tourism.
options.B: To support agriculture.
options.C: To generate electricity.
options.D: To prevent natural disasters.

ev.t: a dam that would control floods, provide irrigation water, and produce hydroelectric power

note: 題目問當初興建水壩的理由，哪一個沒有提到。第 2 段說當初評估興建水壩，是為了防洪（control floods），是 (D) 防止天然災害；提供灌溉用水（provide irrigation water），是 (B) 支援農業；水力發電（produce hydroelectric power），是 (C) 發電。第 4 段雖然說胡佛水壩每年吸引一百多萬名遊客，但那是今天的情況，不是當初興建的理由，所以選 (A)。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about Hoover Dam?

options.A: Its construction lasted for more than a decade.
options.B: It is strong in functionality, but plain in design.
options.C: Its site stretches over two states in the United States.
options.D: It became famous because it led to the discovery of Black Canyon.

ev.t: Located in Black Canyon straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona

note: 第 1 段說胡佛水壩所在的黑峽谷橫跨內華達州和亞利桑那州的州界（straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona），選項換成 stretches over two states，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 Black Canyon，原文沒有說水壩讓人發現了黑峽谷，第 2 段說早在 1900 年左右就有人在評估黑峽谷；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 plain，太平淡的是最初的設計，後來已經請建築師重新設計；(A) 水壩在 1931 年到 1936 年興建，只花了五年左右，不到十年。
map: straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona

stem: According to the passage, what did Six Companies, Inc. experience in the process of building the dam?

options.A: It was defeated by the harsh working conditions.
options.B: It lost some workers in the construction of the dam.
options.C: It benefited from prior experience of building dams of similar scale.
options.D: It gave up the project authorized by the government before the deadline.

ev.t: cost over one hundred lives
The winning bid to build the dam was submitted by Six Companies, Inc.

note: 這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 1 段說興建工程有超過一百人喪命（cost over one hundred lives），第 2 段說得標興建水壩的就是 Six Companies，所以 Six Companies 在興建過程中失去了一些工人，是 (B)。(A) 第 2 段雖然說夏天酷熱、工地缺乏設施，但接著用 Nevertheless 轉折，說 Six Companies 還是完工了，可見並沒有因為困難而放棄；(C) 原文說這麼大的混凝土結構以前沒有人蓋過，所以不可能有類似規模的經驗；(D) 照抄 authorized，國會核准的工程 Six Companies 並沒有放棄，反而提早兩年多完工。

stem: What contribution did Gordon B. Kaufmann make to Hoover Dam?

options.A: He improved the outer appearance of the dam.
options.B: He enhanced the practical functions of the dam.
options.C: He added aboriginal flavor to the design of the floor.
options.D: He decorated the walls of the dam with images from nature.

ev.t: the architect who was brought in to redesign the exterior

note: 第 3 段說最初的設計太平淡，所以請建築師 Kaufmann 重新設計外觀（redesign the exterior），選項換成 improved the outer appearance，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 walls、(C) 照抄 floor，負責牆面和地板裝飾、融入美洲原住民圖像的是插畫家 Allen Tupper True，不是 Kaufmann；(B) 原文說最初的設計太重視功能，Kaufmann 改的是外觀，不是實用功能。

stem: According to the passage, where does the word “restaurant” originate from?

options.A: Famous chefs.
options.B: Popular soups.
options.C: Dining halls.
options.D: Daily menus.

ev.t: the merchant class of Paris developed a taste for healthy clear broths which were considered restorative; hence the term

note: 第 2 段說 1760 年代巴黎的商人愛上了健康的清湯（clear broths），大家認為這種湯能恢復元氣（restorative），hence（因此）restaurant 這個字就是這樣來的。hence 表示這個字是從前面那句來的，前面那句講的是大家都愛喝的清湯，broth 就是湯，選項換成 popular soups，所以是 (B)。restorative 和 restaurant 拼法相近，也看得出兩個字的關係。(C) 照抄 dining halls，1780 年代出現的有名餐廳，是清湯熱潮帶來的結果，不是這個字的來源；(A) 照抄 chefs，中世紀有私人廚師的是貴族，和這個字的來源無關；(D) 原文沒有提到菜單。

stem: What does “taken their toll on kitchen tables” mean in the third paragraph?

options.A: Deprived people of adequate food for living.
options.B: Controlled the nutrients in people’s diet.
options.C: Charged people for using kitchen tables.
options.D: Paid tribute to chefs working in kitchens.

ev.t: the majority of the French population could not afford bread
By 1789, the starving French masses could no longer be controlled.

note: take a toll on 是「對……造成嚴重的不良影響」，kitchen tables 指每戶人家的餐桌，也就是一般人家吃的東西。前一句說大多數法國人連麵包都買不起（could not afford bread），後面又說飢餓的群眾（the starving French masses）失控，可見嚴冬和苛稅讓人民沒有足夠的食物，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 kitchen tables，toll 雖然也有「通行費」的意思，但這裡不是說使用餐桌要收費；(D) 照抄 chefs，第 3 段的廚師是貴族留下來的，和這句話無關；(B) 原文沒有提到營養。

stem: Which of the following is true about commercial diners before the French Revolution?

options.A: Many fine restaurants were owned by highly skilled chefs.
options.B: Reputable dining halls were popular in Paris during the 1760s.
options.C: Public dining halls in the Middle Ages were run-down and dirty.
options.D: A limited variety of food was served in Parisian restaurants in the 1780s.

ev.t: The only commercial diners for the masses were dusty, shabby roadside inns

note: 第 2 段說中世紀時，一般大眾唯一能去的營業用餐處所，是塵土滿布（dusty）、破舊簡陋（shabby）的路邊旅店，選項換成 run-down and dirty，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 Reputable dining halls，有名的餐廳是 1780 年代才出現的，1760 年代巴黎商人才剛愛上清湯；(D) 照抄 1780s，原文說那時候的餐廳可以從許多菜色中挑選，菜色不是有限；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 highly skilled chefs，技術高超的廚師原本替貴族工作，大革命以後才流向城裡的餐館，原文也沒有說餐廳是廚師開的。

stem: What was the main reason for Napoleon to promote the development of restaurants?

options.A: He hoped to improve the life of his citizens.
options.B: He wanted to help unemployed chefs find new jobs.
options.C: He feared that reductions in restaurants might hurt the travel business.
options.D: He believed that the development of restaurants would bring political stability.

ev.t: as he reasoned that people who were focused on champagne and fine food probably would not conspire against him

note: 第 4 段說拿破崙給公民「享樂的自由」，因為他認為一心想著香檳和美食的人，大概不會密謀推翻他（would not conspire against him）。沒有人密謀推翻他，政權就穩定，所以是 (D)。(A) 讓公民享樂看起來像是為人民著想，但原文用 as 點出真正的理由是保住自己的政權；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 unemployed，失業的廚師進城開店是大革命時期的事，在拿破崙掌權以前；(C) 照抄 travel，旅遊指南只是用來說明餐廳的數量增加，原文沒有提到餐廳減少會影響旅遊業。

stem: What makes falcons a unique animal for hunting in Islamic culture?

options.A: Falcons are relatively easy to train for hunting.
options.B: Falcons can form a strong bond with their owners quickly.
options.C: Falcons’ vision is particularly suitable for hunting in deserts.
options.D: Falcons keep their prey alive before delivering it to falconers.

ev.t: they can be trained to deliver their prey, without killing it first.
animals used for food must still be alive

note: 第 3 段說獵鷹經過訓練，可以把獵物帶回來，不先殺死（without killing it first），這在伊斯蘭文化很重要，因為當作食物的動物必須還活著，肉才是清真的。選項換成 keep their prey alive，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 vision，獵鷹的視力是人類的 2.6 倍，但這和伊斯蘭文化的規定無關；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 strong，緊密的關係是鷹獵者日夜和獵鷹住在一起建立的，原文沒有說很快就能建立；(A) 第 2 段說先不給食物，是讓獵鷹比較容易馴服，原文沒有說獵鷹本來就比較好訓練，也和伊斯蘭文化無關。

stem: What is the main reason for Arabic people to hunt with falcons today?

options.A: To supplement their diet.
options.B: To serve as entertainment and exercise.
options.C: To worship their national bird.
options.D: To replace the practice of hunting with dogs.

ev.t: But now, it has become the favorite sport and pastime in the Arabian Peninsula.

note: 第 1 段說鷹獵過去是為了補充食物，But now（不過現在）已經成為阿拉伯半島最受歡迎的運動（sport）和休閒活動（pastime），選項換成 entertainment and exercise，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 supplement，補充食物是過去的目的，題目問的是今天（today）；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 national bird，有些國家把獵鷹定為國鳥，原文沒有說打獵是為了崇拜國鳥；(D) 照抄 dogs，「天空獵犬」（hunting dogs of the skies）是比喻獵鷹的說法，原文沒有說用獵鷹取代獵犬。

stem: According to the article, what privilege do falcons enjoy in the Arab world?

options.A: Free air ticket.
options.B: Passports issued by the King.
options.C: Meals that are halal.
options.D: Access to specialized medical care.

ev.t: specialist hospitals have been established to take care of these magnificent birds

note: 第 4 段說鷹獵越來越受歡迎，甚至有專門照顧獵鷹的醫院（specialist hospitals），選項換成 specialized medical care，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)，這個選項照抄 Passports，但原文只說獵鷹還能領到自己的護照（are even issued their own passports），沒有說護照是誰發的，選項加上的 by the King，原文沒有這個資訊。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 halal，清真講的是獵鷹抓回來、要給人吃的獵物，不是獵鷹自己吃的餐點；(A) 原文說獵鷹可以合法搭飛機、待在機艙裡，沒有說機票免費。

stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Falconers deprive the falcons of food in order to capture them.
options.B: Falcons are not allowed to see their masters during the training process.
options.C: The trainers’ names are imprinted on the hoods covering the birds’ heads.
options.D: Wild falcons with natural hunting skills are most ideal for falconers to catch.

ev.t: The best birds to catch are the ones with naturally nurtured hunting skills, aged one or two years.

note: 第 2 段說最適合捕捉的（The best birds to catch）是一、兩歲、天生就有狩獵本領（naturally nurtured hunting skills）的獵鷹，選項換成 most ideal for falconers to catch，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 of food，不給食物是捉到以後的訓練步驟，目的是讓獵鷹容易馴服，不是為了捕捉；(C) 照抄 imprint，原文的 imprint 是獵鷹把第一眼看到的人認作主人，不是把名字印在頭罩上；(B) 照抄 master，原文說鷹獵者日夜和獵鷹住在一起，訓練時並沒有不讓獵鷹看到主人。
map: most ideal for falconers to catch

stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the first paragraph?

options.A: Science and technology have influenced the game of golf.
options.B: Price, durability, and function determine the quality of golf balls.
options.C: Accumulated efforts have resulted in changes in how golf balls are made.
options.D: Golfers who have a sound knowledge of aerodynamics play the game well.

ev.t: many advances have occurred in the game, including significant changes to the golf ball.

note: 第 1 段第一句說高爾夫球這項運動有了許多進步，其中包括球本身的重大改變（significant changes to the golf ball），接著依時間順序介紹木球、羽毛球、古塔膠球、Haskell 球、有凹洞的球，一直到現在的球。一代一代累積的改良，改變了球的製作方式，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 2 段的 aerodynamics，空氣動力是第 2 段的內容，第 1 段沒有談；(A) 科學和科技影響高爾夫球運動，說得太籠統，第 1 段只談球的演進；(B) 價格、耐用度只是用來比較各代的球，第 1 段沒有說這些條件決定球的品質。
map: significant changes to the golf ball
changes in how golf balls are made

stem: Which of the following is true about golf balls?

options.A: William Taylor added a rubber center to golf balls.
options.B: The Gutta Percha ball was stuffed with bird feathers.
options.C: The Featherie was the first golf ball ever used in the game.
options.D: The Haskell lasted longer and traveled farther than its predecessor.

ev.t: The Haskell traveled up to 20 yards farther than the Gutta Percha ball and was more durable.

note: 第 1 段說 Haskell 球比之前的古塔膠球多飛 20 碼（traveled up to 20 yards farther），也更耐用（more durable），選項換成 lasted longer and traveled farther than its predecessor，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 rubber，第一顆有橡膠核心的是 Haskell 球，William Taylor 推出的是第一顆有凹洞的球；(B) 照抄 feathers，塞羽毛的是羽毛球，古塔膠球的原料是古塔樹葉子的汁液；(C) 照抄 Featherie，羽毛球之前已經有圓形木球，羽毛球不是最早的高爾夫球。

stem: How do dimples on a golf ball affect its performance?

options.A: They help it travel farther.
options.B: They keep it in a better shape.
options.C: They enhance its drag force.
options.D: They allow it to endure stronger impact.

ev.t: With dimples added to the ball, the force that pulls back on the ball is minimized, allowing it to travel faster and longer.

note: 第 2 段說球加上凹洞以後，往後拉的力量減到最小，讓球飛得更快、更遠（travel faster and longer），選項換成 travel farther，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 drag，往後拉的力量就是阻力（drag），凹洞把阻力減到最小，選項說增加阻力，剛好相反；(B) 保持形狀、(D) 承受更強的撞擊，原文都沒有提到。

stem: Which ball will give golfers a better shot to get a ball out of a deep sand trap?

options.A: A ball with deep dimples.
options.B: A ball made from Gutta trees.
options.C: A ball with a leather sack.
options.D: A ball with a smooth outer cover.

ev.t: whereas those with deeper dimples have a higher flight path.

note: 球掉進很深的沙坑，要讓球飛得高，才打得出來。第 2 段說凹洞比較深的球（deeper dimples），飛行路徑比較高，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Gutta、(C) 照抄 leather sack，古塔膠球和塞羽毛的皮囊球都是舊式的球，原文沒有說它們適合打沙坑；(D) 照抄 outer cover，Haskell 球有外殼，但原文說凹洞才影響飛行高度，表面光滑的球沒有凹洞的好處。

stem: Who is most likely the writer of this passage?

options.A: The President of the University of Illinois.
options.B: A movie critic who is a friend of the Eberts.
options.C: A member of the Festival’s organizing committee.
options.D: A journalist who reports stories about the Festival.

ev.t: In selecting the films for this year, Chaz Ebert and I looked to women filmmakers for our inspiration.
We would like to thank our sponsors, volunteers, festival pass holders, and individual ticket holders

note: 作者在第 2 段說今年選片時，Chaz Ebert 和我（Chaz Ebert and I）以女性電影人作為靈感，可見作者負責挑選影片；第 4 段又代表影展感謝贊助者、志工和觀眾，全文也一直用 our festival、we 這樣的說法。會選片、會代表影展致謝的，最可能是影展籌備委員會的成員，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 University of Illinois，作者是在感謝伊利諾大學，不是代表大學說話；(D) 記者是報導影展的外人，不會說「我們的影展」；(B) 作者說能和伊伯特夫婦合作是一種榮幸，是合作的關係，原文沒有說作者是影評人。

stem: What was the purpose of reinventing Roger Ebert’s Film Festival in 1999?

options.A: To work closely with the University of Illinois.
options.B: To help restore a building associated with the Festival.
options.C: To establish a signature annual event in the community.
options.D: To honor people who made films that were not box-office hits.

ev.t: to make a festival that celebrated overlooked films, formats and genres, and the women and men who made those films

note: 第 1 段說 1999 年重新打造影展，是要表揚少有人注意的電影（overlooked films），以及拍出這些電影的人。少有人注意的電影，就是票房不好、沒什麼人看的片子，所以是 (D)。這一句是倒裝：Little did we think（我們萬萬沒想到）後面接的，是當初沒有料到的結果，不是目的。(C) 照抄 annual event，成為社區的年度盛事，(B) 幫忙修復 Virginia 戲院，都是當時沒有料到的結果；(A) 照抄 University of Illinois，伊利諾大學媒體學院是合作單位，原文沒有說合作是重新打造影展的目的。

stem: What is the focus of this year’s film selection?

options.A: Films produced or directed by women.
options.B: Hollywood classics and legends.
options.C: Stories featuring female leading roles.
options.D: Diversity in formats and genres.

ev.t: Chaz Ebert and I looked to women filmmakers for our inspiration.
Fully half of our films are either directed or co-directed by women, and several others have women in powerful producing roles.

note: 第 2 段說今年選片以女性電影人（women filmmakers）作為靈感，一半的影片由女性執導或共同執導，還有好幾部由女性擔任製片，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 roles，原文的 producing roles 是幕後的製片工作，不是片中的女主角；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 Hollywood，好萊塢傳奇人物 Jeff Dowd 是嘉賓，不是選片重點；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 formats and genres，那是 1999 年重新打造影展時要表揚的對象，不是今年選片的重點。

stem: Which of the following is NOT included in the writer’s acknowledgement remarks?

options.A: The founder of Roger Ebert’s Film Festival.
options.B: A student who purchased a pass to the Festival.
options.C: The producer of the Festival’s award-winning film.
options.D: A company which provided financial support for the Festival.

ev.t: We would like to thank our sponsors, volunteers, festival pass holders, and individual ticket holders
for that we thank him and his wife Chaz.

note: 作者在第 4、5 段致謝。感謝贊助者（sponsors），是 (D) 出錢支持影展的公司；感謝影展通行證持有人（festival pass holders），買了通行證的學生也在其中，是 (B)；第 5 段感謝羅傑·伊伯特，影展是他送給家鄉的禮物，他就是 (A) 影展的創辦人。第 2 段雖然提到幾位女性製片，但那是介紹今年的選片，不是致謝，原文也沒有提到哪一部片子得獎，所以選 (C)。

stem: What is the second paragraph mainly about?

options.A: General facts regarding storm chasing.
options.B: Common equipment used by storm chasers.
options.C: Shared characteristics among storm chasers.
options.D: Meteorological knowledge crucial to storm chasing.

ev.t: Chasing often involves driving thousands of miles in order to witness a relatively short window of time of severe weather.
The amount of equipment used for storm chasing also varies.

note: 第 2 段講了好幾件追風暴的一般情況：常要開幾千英里的車，空手而回並不少見；大部分人不是專業的氣象學家；使用的裝備多寡也各不相同。這一段介紹的是追風暴的一般事實，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 equipment，裝備只是這一段的其中一件事；(D) 氣象學也只占一句，原文是說很多人花時間自學，不是在介紹氣象知識；(C) 這一段反而一再說各人不同，有人只帶攝影器材，有人什麼都用上，講的不是共同點。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about chasing severe weather?

options.A: The danger of chasing tornadoes can be avoided.
options.B: Those who chase storms share one common reason.
options.C: There is a standard set of equipment for storm chasing.
options.D: Core punching is a necessary component of storm chasing.

ev.t: Tornadoes affect a relatively small area and are predictable enough to be avoided if a safe distance is maintained.

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The traditional Māori haka is limited to use by male Māori warriors in battle.
options.B: The original meaning of haka in Māori is a war dance accompanied by songs.
options.C: The All Blacks have taken turns performing Ka Mate and Kapa o Pango since 1906.
options.D: Haka are now used for important events by both Māori and non-Māori New Zealanders.

ev.t: different varieties of haka are performed on various ceremonial occasions
and New Zealanders of European heritage alike view doing the haka with a sense of pride

note: 最後一段說現在哈卡在迎接貴賓、婚禮、葬禮等典禮場合（ceremonial occasions）表演，而且毛利人和歐洲裔的紐西蘭人（New Zealanders of European heritage）都以跳哈卡為榮。選項把典禮場合換成 important events，把歐洲裔的紐西蘭人換成 non-Māori New Zealanders，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄最後一段的 limited to，傳統上只限於毛利社群，不是只限男性戰士，第 2 段還說有些哈卡男女都能跳，甚至有只限女性的；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 war dance，那是一般人的看法，接著 But 一轉，說在毛利語中 haka 只是「舞蹈」的意思；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 1906，1906 年全黑隊第一次表演的是 Ka Mate，Kapa o Pango 是 2005 年才寫的，不可能從 1906 年起就輪流表演。

stem: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?

options.A: Computers and Assessments
options.B: The Four Components of ESSA
options.C: Student-Centered Curriculum and Instruction
options.D: From NCLB to ESSA, with a Focus on Assessment

note: 第 1 段先說 ESSA 取代了 NCLB，讓各州在課程、教學、評量上有更多決定權，最後一句說 Below are some big-picture ideas influencing many states as they approach the assessment task，點出後面要談的是各州規劃評量（assessment）的方向；第 2 到 5 段依序談彈性、多科目測驗、重視學習過程、評量的目的，四段都在講評量。標題要同時涵蓋從 NCLB 換成 ESSA，以及談的重點是評量，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)：後面四段是影響各州的四個大方向（ideas influencing many states），不是 ESSA 這個法案的四個組成部分，偏離主題。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 student-centered，全文談的是評量，不是課程和教學，偏離主題；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 computer，電腦適性測驗只是第 2 段舉的例子，過於狹隘。

stem: What does the word “dilemma” in paragraph 2 refer to?

options.A: The choice between SAT and ACT.
options.B: The choice between NCLB and ESSA.
options.C: Whether or not to use student-centered assessment.
options.D: Whether or not to replace computer-based assessment.

ev.t: Thus, states are rethinking one-size-fits-all standardized assessments and are instead considering personalized, student-centered assessments in schools.
Obviously, the task is difficult and time-consuming.

note: 第 2 段先說標準化評量容易使用，卻無法完整呈現學生的進展，所以各州考慮改用以學生為中心的評量（student-centered assessments）；接著說這項工作既困難又費時。一邊是比較完整的評量，一邊是做起來很難，要不要採用以學生為中心的評量，就是這裡的 dilemma（難題），所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 SAT and ACT，那是拿來比喻標準化評量的例子，不是要在兩者之間做選擇；(D) 照抄 computer，電腦適性測驗是解決難題的方法，不是難題本身；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 NCLB，2015 年 ESSA 就已經取代了 NCLB，這是已經決定的事。

stem: Which of the following is an emerging new subject in the ESSA assessment?

options.A: Math.
options.B: Reading.
options.C: Science.
options.D: Economics.

ev.t: some are now starting to include social studies, government, or economics.

note: 題目問的是新興（emerging）的科目，要把第 3 段提到的科目分成舊的和新的。第 3 段說數學和閱讀是傳統（traditional）科目，(A)、(B) 都不是新的；自然科學是全部 50 個州都已經至少考兩次的科目，(C) 也不是新的；接著說有些州現在才開始（now starting to）加考社會、公民或經濟，所以新興的科目是 (D) Economics。(A) 照抄 math、(B) 照抄 reading、(C) 照抄 science，三個字都在第 3 段，但都是已經在考的科目。

stem:
If the following sentences were to be included in the passage, which paragraph should they go to?
One good example is that many teachers today are asking students to keep a learning portfolio, which is a purposeful collection of student works at different points of time in the semester. This portfolio exhibits students’ effort, progress, and achievements in one or more areas of the course.

options.A: Paragraph 2.
options.B: Paragraph 3.
options.C: Paragraph 4.
options.D: Paragraph 5.

ev.t: Teachers are encouraged to accumulate data at different points in their students
These data together present a more complete picture of a student

note: 要插入的兩句說，現在很多老師要學生建立學習歷程檔案，蒐集學期中不同時間點（at different points of time）的作品，呈現學生的努力、進步和成就。第 4 段說各州重視學習過程，老師在學生學習過程的不同時間點（at different points）累積資料，這些資料合起來，能更完整地呈現學生的學習。學習歷程檔案正是第 4 段這個做法的例子，所以插入句開頭說 One good example，放在第 4 段，是 (C)。(A) 第 2 段講的是彈性和電腦適性測驗；(B) 第 3 段講的是多科目測驗；(D) 第 5 段講的是評量的目的，都和不同時間點蒐集作品接不上。

stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: The preparation of a health food.
options.B: A traditional delicacy from Java.
options.C: A gourmet guide for vegetarians.
options.D: The cultural heritage of Indonesia.

note: 第 1 段介紹天貝是印尼的傳統食物，第 2–5 段依序講源自爪哇的起源、營養、料理方式和文化價值，所以全文介紹的是一種來自爪哇的傳統美食。(A) 料理方式只講第 4 段，(C) 素食者只在第 3 段提到，都過於狹隘；(D) 印尼的文化遺產範圍比天貝大得多，第 5 段只說天貝有機會列入，太過廣泛。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about tempeh?

options.A: It is mainly served as a side dish.
options.B: It is discarded when fungi grow around it.
options.C: It is formed from fermented soybeans.
options.D: It has the same nutritional benefits as kimchi.

ev.t: tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java
It was discovered during tofu production when discarded soybean residue caught microbial spores from the air and grew certain whitish fungi around it.

note: 天貝是豆渣沾上微生物發酵而成的食物，也就是由發酵的大豆做成。(B) 照抄 discarded 和 fungi，但丟棄的是豆渣，長出真菌後反而變成天貝；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 side dish，但天貝也可以當主菜、點心；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 kimchi，那只是拿來比喻同樣是國家的代表食物。

stem: What aspects of tempeh are discussed in paragraphs 2 to 4?

options.A: Origin → nutrition → cuisine.
options.B: Origin → cuisine → marketing.
options.C: Cuisine → nutrition → marketing.
options.D: Distribution → cuisine → nutrition.

ev.t: tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java
Tempeh is high in protein and low in fat, and contains a host of vitamins.
In addition to its highly nutritional makeup, tempeh has diverse preparation possibilities.

note: 看每段的第一句就能抓出重點：第 2 段源自爪哇，第 3 段營養成分，第 4 段料理方式。第 4 段開頭 In addition to its highly nutritional makeup 先回顧上一段的營養，再轉到料理，正好把兩段接起來。(B)、(C) 的 marketing 文章沒有談，(B) 又把第 3 段的營養說成料理，(C) 把第 2 段的由來說成料理；(D) 的 distribution 可以對上第 2 段後半天貝傳遍印尼各地，但後面兩項順序顛倒，第 3 段才是營養、第 4 段才是料理。
map: originating from the island of Java
high in protein and low in fat

stem: Which of the following can be inferred from this passage?

options.A: Senior citizens will eat tempeh as vitamin supplement.
options.B: Tempeh will soon be more popular than kimchi or miso.
options.C: The nutrition of tempeh will be reduced with mass production.
options.D: Tempeh is likely to be recognized as an international cultural symbol.

ev.t: With the Indonesian traditional fabric batik being recognized by UNESCO as “Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity,” tempeh has great potential for this honor as well.

note: 蠟染已經列入人類非物質文化遺產，天貝也很有希望得到這項殊榮，換個說法就是很可能成為國際認可的文化象徵。(B) 照抄 kimchi，文章沒有比較誰比較受歡迎，還說天貝在國際上不算熱門；(A) 照抄 vitamin，文章沒提年長者；(C) 第 2 段說天貝是各地人家自己在家做的，文章沒有談大量生產，也沒說營養會因此減少。
map: has great potential for this honor

stem: How does the author begin the passage?

options.A: By giving a definition.
options.B: By mentioning an incident.
options.C: By providing statistics.
options.D: By comparing people’s responses.

ev.t: When Dr. David Spiegel emerged from a three-hour shoulder surgery in 1972

note: 第 1 段一開頭講一件事：1972 年 Spiegel 醫師動完肩部手術，沒有用止痛藥，而是替自己催眠，結果真的有效。作者用一件實際發生的事開場，引出催眠這個主題，所以是 (B)。(A) 催眠的定義在第 2 段才出現；(C) 第 4 段才有止痛藥用量減半的研究結果，開頭沒有統計數字；(D) 比較兩組人的反應是第 3 段的研究。

stem: According to the passage, what is the goal of Dr. Spiegel’s work?

options.A: To explain the real cause of pain.
options.B: To help people concentrate on their job.
options.C: To explore how hypnosis can be used as a medical treatment.
options.D: To strengthen the brain’s functions to reduce psychological problems.

ev.t: This trance-like state can be an effective tool to control pain, ease anxiety, and deal with stress.
Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers.

note: 第 2 段說催眠是控制疼痛、緩解焦慮、應付壓力的有效工具；第 4 段說 Spiegel 希望催眠可以用來取代止痛藥（replace painkillers），還研究了自我催眠能讓病人少用一半的止痛藥。他研究的是催眠怎麼當作醫療方法，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 pain，他研究的是用催眠減輕疼痛，不是找出疼痛的原因；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 brain，研究人員只是觀察到催眠時大腦的變化，沒有說要強化大腦的功能；(B) 第 2 段的專注是說明催眠時的狀態，不是要幫人專心工作。

stem: According to Dr. Spiegel, which of the following is true when people are hypnotized?

options.A: They recall only happy memories.
options.B: Their mind is fixed only on what they are doing.
options.C: They do whatever they are told to do.
options.D: They have greater awareness of things around them.

ev.t: You focus intently on the subject at hand, to the near exclusion of any other thought.

note: 第 2 段先說一般人的誤解（is often misunderstood as），再用 But according to Dr. Spiegel 帶出他的看法。題目問的是 According to Dr. Spiegel，答案要在 But 後面找：催眠時你會全神貫注在眼前的事情上（focus intently on the subject at hand），幾乎不去想別的事，選項換成 Their mind is fixed only on what they are doing，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 whatever，別人叫你做什麼就做什麼，是 But 前面一般人的誤解；(D) 照抄 around，原文說催眠時會把周遭（around you）大部分的刺激屏除在外，選項說更能察覺周遭的事物，意思正好相反；(A) 第 3 段的回想記憶，是研究中掃描大腦的其中一種情況，不是催眠時的狀態，原文也沒有提到快樂的記憶。
map: focus intently on the subject at hand
fixed only on what they are doing

stem: What can be inferred about highly hypnotizable people?

options.A: They tend to be isolated from the society.
options.B: They are more likely to fall asleep during the day.
options.C: They may easily identify themselves with characters in fictions.
options.D: They are more trustworthy than people who are less hypnotizable.

ev.t: more likely to get caught up in a good movie.

note: 第 3 段說容易催眠的人，看到一部好電影，比較容易沉浸其中（get caught up in a good movie）。看電影容易入戲，就是容易把自己投入片中角色的處境，電影也是虛構的故事，選項換成 identify themselves with characters in fictions，所以是 (C)。最容易選錯的是 (D)，這個選項照抄 trust：原文說的是容易催眠的人比較信任別人（more trusting of others），trusting 是「信任別人」，選項的 trustworthy 是「值得別人信任」，兩個字意思不同。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 sleep，把催眠當成睡著，正是 Spiegel 說的誤解；(A) 容易催眠的人比較信任別人，看不出他們和社會隔絕。
map: caught up in a good movie

stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To evaluate the languages used by different ethnic groups.
options.B: To prove how civilization slows down language development.
options.C: To describe how terms of smell are found in different languages.
options.D: To point out the link between language use and the environment.

note: 第 1、2 段比較英語和 Maniq 語、Jahai 語描述氣味的詞彙；第 3 段說英語的困難和鼻子的能力無關，研究人員認為是環境的關係；第 4 段說明兩種生活環境的差異，最後說這個差異或許能解釋這個語言現象。全文要指出的是語言使用和環境之間的關係，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 terms，介紹各種語言有多少氣味詞彙，只是第 2 段的內容，全文還要解釋原因，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ethnic groups，原文沒有評價哪一種語言比較好，偏離主題；(B) 原文說英語使用者不必靠氣味生存，沒有說文明讓語言發展變慢，偏離主題。

stem: What does the word “want” in the first paragraph most likely mean?

options.A: Lack.
options.B: Growth.
options.C: Loss.
options.D: Search.

ev.t: For want of dedicated odor terminology, English speakers are often forced to use odor-sources

note: for want of 是固定片語，意思是「因為缺少」，want 在這裡當名詞用。從上下文也推得出來：第 1 段第一句說英語沒有直截了當談論氣味的方法，後面說英語使用者只好（are forced to）借用氣味的來源和比喻。只好借用別的說法，是因為缺少專門的氣味詞彙，所以 want 最接近 (A) Lack。(C) Loss 是「失去」，表示原本有、後來沒了，原文沒有說英語曾經有這些詞彙；(B) 成長、(D) 尋找，都接不上後面的「只好借用」。

stem: Which of the following is true about the Maniq?

options.A: They live in a different climate zone from the Jahai.
options.B: Their ability to smell is stronger than that of the Jahai.
options.C: They use smell terms to describe how food looks and tastes.
options.D: Their living environment is similar to that in earlier human history.

ev.t: Maniq and Jahai speakers live in tropical rainforest regions with a hunting-gathering lifestyle
In an environment that is still largely untouched by humans

note: 第 4 段說 Maniq 人住在熱帶雨林，過著狩獵採集的生活，而且環境大部分仍未經人類開發（still largely untouched by humans）。以打獵、採集維生，住在沒有開發的大自然裡，和人類早期的生活環境相似，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 smell，原文說兩個族群都靠嗅覺生存，沒有比較誰的嗅覺比較好；(C) 照抄 food，腐壞的食物是他們要用嗅覺察覺的危險，第 2 段也說這些氣味詞只用來表達氣味，不能用在其他感官上，不會拿來描述食物的外觀和味道；(A) 兩個族群是鄰居，第 4 段說兩者都住在熱帶雨林，氣候帶相同。
map: similar to that in earlier human history

stem: Why is it difficult for English speakers to describe smells directly?

options.A: They cannot distinguish the smells around them.
options.B: The sense of smell is not critical for their survival.
options.C: They consider it uncivilized to talk about smells directly.
options.D: There are not many sources of odor in their surroundings.

ev.t: do not rely on smells to survive in their environment.

note: 第 4 段說很多說英語的人住在後工業化的西方，不必靠氣味（do not rely on smells）就能在環境中生存，這個差異或許能解釋英語缺少氣味詞彙的現象。選項換成 The sense of smell is not critical for their survival，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 3 段的 surroundings，研究人員說的是環境扮演重要的角色，原因在於要不要靠氣味生存，不是環境裡的氣味來源少；(A) 第 3 段說說英語的人能分辨超過一兆種氣味，所以不是分辨不出來；(C) 原文沒有說談論氣味不文明。
map: do not rely on smells to survive

stem: Which of the following is a picture of an okapi?

options.A: （見圖）
options.B: （見圖）
options.C: （見圖）
options.D: （見圖）

figure.source: 大學入學考試中心 108 學年度指定科目考試英文考科

ev.t: The coat is a chocolate to reddish brown, much in contrast with the white horizontal stripes and rings on the legs and white ankles.
the fleeting view of the striped backside

note: 第 2 段說霍加狓身上的毛是巧克力色到紅棕色，白色的橫紋和環紋長在腿上，腳踝是白色的；第 3 段也說探險家瞥見的是牠帶條紋的臀部。條紋在腿和臀部、身體是深色的毛、腳踝是白色，四張圖裡只有 (B) 符合。(A)、(C) 的條紋畫在身體前半部的軀幹上，不在腿上；(D) 雖然後腿有條紋，身體中段卻是淺色，不是巧克力色到紅棕色，頭上還長著像鹿一樣分岔的大角，原文說霍加狓只是外觀像鹿，沒有說牠有這種角，(A) 也一樣。

stem: Which of the following descriptions is true about the okapi?

options.A: It is an important symbol of Congo.
options.B: It is a mystical creature from a Greek legend.
options.C: It has been well protected since 1987.
options.D: It is more closely related to the zebra than the giraffe.

ev.t: Yet its image is prevalent in the Democratic Republic of Congo
The okapi is to Congo what the giant panda is to China or the kangaroo to Australia.

note: 第 1 段說在剛果，霍加狓的形象隨處可見（its image is prevalent），又說霍加狓之於剛果，就像大貓熊之於中國、袋鼠之於澳洲。大貓熊、袋鼠都是代表一個國家的動物，所以霍加狓是剛果重要的象徵，是 (A)。(B) 照抄 Greek legend，原文用 as if 說「好像」希臘神話裡的生物，是比喻，霍加狓是真實存在的動物；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 1987，那一年設立了保護區，但後來政治動盪，霍加狓的數量減少了一半，不能說從那時起一直保護得很好；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 zebra，原文說霍加狓的條紋像斑馬，親緣關係卻和長頸鹿最近，選項說反了。

stem: What does the word “whiff” most likely mean in the third paragraph?

options.A: Firm belief.
options.B: Kind intention.
options.C: Slight trace.
options.D: Strong dislike.

ev.t: The West got its first whiff of the okapi in 1890 when Welsh journalist Henry Morton Stanley had puzzled over a strange
Explorers may have seen the fleeting view of the striped backside

note: whiff 原本是「一陣氣味」，引申為一點點跡象或風聲。從上下文也推得出來：第 3 段說 1890 年 Stanley 只是在書裡提到一種讓他百思不解的「非洲驢」，連那是什麼動物都不知道；探險家可能也只瞥見一閃而過的條紋臀部。西方第一次得到的，只是一點點線索，所以 whiff 最接近 (C) Slight trace。(A) 堅定的信念，和 Stanley 的百思不解正好相反；(B) 善意、(D) 強烈的厭惡，都和認識霍加狓這件事接不上。

stem: Which of the following can be inferred about Henry Morton Stanley?

options.A: He was the first European to analyze okapi skeleton.
options.B: He had found many new species of animals in Africa.
options.C: He did not know the “African donkey” in his book was the okapi.
options.D: He had seen the backside of an okapi dashing through the bushes.

ev.t: Henry Morton Stanley had puzzled over a strange

note: 第 3 段說 Stanley 在書裡提到一種讓他百思不解（had puzzled over）的奇怪「非洲驢」。他對這種動物感到困惑，可見他並不知道那就是霍加狓，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 skeleton，分析骨骸的是後來的博物學家；(D) 照抄 backside，瞥見條紋臀部的是探險家，而且原文用 may have seen，只是推測；(B) 照抄 new species，有人以為霍加狓是新的斑馬，原文沒有說 Stanley 在非洲發現了很多新物種。

stem: Which of the following titles best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.B: Fundraising for Music Companies
options.C: Music Fans Profiting from Investments

note: 第 1 段用英國樂團 SVM 的例子，帶出 MMC 用群眾募資替藝人籌錢；第 2 段說明運作方式；第 3 段說 MMC 和一般群眾募資有什麼不同；第 4 段說唱片公司不敢冒險，群眾募資能分散風險，讓更多唱片製作出來。全文講的是音樂產業的群眾募資，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (B)，這個選項照抄第 4 段的 music companies：原文說募來的錢用來替旗下的藝人（its acts）錄音，籌錢的對象是藝人，不是唱片公司，第 4 段還說唱片公司變得不敢冒險，偏離主題。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 Web-based，網路是募資的管道，全文談的是籌錢，不是用網路製作音樂，偏離主題；(C) 投資人拿到高額回報，只是第 2 段的一個例子，過於狹隘。

stem: How much money does a band have to raise via MMC to have their music recorded?

ev.t: Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording

ev.t: Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200.

note: a long shot 是「希望渺茫的事」。這一句用 While 對比：雖然數位科技讓音樂人掀起自己動手做的風潮，要成功仍然……；下一句接著說，2009 年美國發行的兩萬張唱片中，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名。成功的比例這麼低，可見成功並不容易，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 shot、(D) 照抄 long，都是把片語拆開來照字面解釋；(A) 成功的效果持久，和下一句的數字接不上。

stem: Why did Tsar Alexander III choose Peter Fabergé to make the first Easter egg?

options.A: Peter Fabergé was the goldsmith for the royal family.
options.B: Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work.
options.C: Tsar Alexander III received an order from Empress Maria.
options.D: Peter Fabergé owned the most famous Russian jewelry house.

ev.t: whose beautiful creations had caught Maria

note: 第 2 段說沙皇向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，因為他美麗的作品（beautiful creations）先前就吸引了（had caught）瑪麗亞的目光，選項換成 Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 goldsmith，法貝熱是在第一顆彩蛋讓皇后滿意以後，才獲得皇室特約金匠的頭銜；(C) 照抄 order，下訂單的是沙皇，選項說沙皇接到皇后的訂單，說反了；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 famous Russian，法貝熱公司是後來才成為著名的珠寶商，沙皇訂製時，第 2 段說他還是年輕的珠寶師。

stem: What went missing from the first Fabergé egg?

options.A: A golden hen and a ruby egg.
options.B: A golden hen and a golden yolk.
options.C: A ruby egg and a diamond crown.
options.D: A golden yolk and a diamond crown.

ev.t: concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg.
Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.

note: 第 2 段依序說蛋打開來是金蛋黃，蛋黃裡有金母雞，母雞裡藏著鑽石小皇冠（a diamond miniature of the royal crown）和紅寶石小蛋（a tiny ruby egg），接著說最後兩樣驚喜（the last two surprises）已經失傳。最後兩樣就是鑽石皇冠和紅寶石蛋，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 golden hen、(B) 和 (D) 照抄 golden yolk，金母雞和金蛋黃是前面兩樣，沒有失傳。
map: diamond miniature of the royal crown

stem: What does it mean by “Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge” in the third paragraph?

options.A: They repeated their designs over and over.
options.B: They fulfilled the Tsar’s requirements each time.
options.C: They challenged the Tsar’s expectations every year.
options.D: They were faced with unexpected difficulties time and again.

ev.t: The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise.
Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge.

note: 這裡的 meet 不是「遇到」，而是「達成、符合」，meet the challenge 是成功應付挑戰。the challenge 指的是前一句沙皇的要求（The requirements）：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，而且要藏著驚喜；repeatedly 是每年一次又一次。合起來就是法貝熱和繼承人每一次都做到了沙皇的要求，所以是 (B)。(D) 把 meet 當成「遇到」，又把 challenge 當成困難，照字面解釋；(C) 照抄 challenge，挑戰是沙皇給法貝熱的，選項說法貝熱挑戰沙皇，主客顛倒；(A) 照抄 repeated，原文要求每顆彩蛋都獨一無二，不可能重複同樣的設計。

stem: Which of the following statements about the Fabergé eggs is true, according to the passage?

options.A: They were all genuine creations of the jeweler, Peter Fabergé.
options.B: They were created to represent Russian emperors and their dynasty.
options.C: They were made for annual Easter parties in the Russian imperial court.
options.D: They were connected to the last two Russian emperors and their families.

ev.t: for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.
they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.

note: 這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 3 段說法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世做彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止；第 4 段說這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。革命以後俄國就沒有沙皇了，所以這兩位是俄國最後兩位皇帝，彩蛋又是送給皇后等家人的禮物，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Peter Fabergé，第 3 段說彩蛋是他和他的繼承人（his successors）做的，不全是他本人的作品；(C) 照抄 Easter，彩蛋是復活節送給皇后的禮物，原文沒有說是為宮廷的復活節派對做的；(B) 讓人想起俄國最後的皇室，是彩蛋今天的意義，彩蛋當初是沙皇送皇后的禮物，不是為了代表皇帝和王朝而做。

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: The food network in nature.
options.B: The construction of orb webs.
options.C: The network of geometrical studies.

note: 第 1 段說圓網是最美、結構最有秩序的蜘蛛網，並說明網的功能；第 2 段介紹圓網的兩大特點：幾何結構和建造的材料。全文講的是圓網怎麼構成，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 environmental，網要承受風雨，只是第 1 段說明網絲需要多強韌，過於狹隘；(A) 蜘蛛網的功能是捕捉獵物，但全文沒有談自然界的食物網，偏離主題；(C) 第 2 段的幾何結構是在描述網的形狀，不是談幾何學的研究，偏離主題。

stem: What does the word “so” in the first paragraph refer to?

options.A: To catch and keep small creatures.
options.B: To find a good material for the web.
options.C: To observe the behavior patterns of spiders.
options.D: To present a fantastic architecture by animals.

ev.t: The main function of the web is to intercept and hold flying prey

note: In order to do so 的 do so 指的是前一句說的事：蜘蛛網的主要功能是攔住並困住（intercept and hold）蒼蠅、蜜蜂等飛行的獵物，讓蜘蛛有時間抓住。選項把飛行的獵物換成 small creatures，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 architecture，動物建築是第 1 段第一句的開場；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 material，網的材料是後面才談的特點；(C) 原文沒有提到觀察蜘蛛的行為。

stem: Which part of the web is used for supporting the web itself?

options.A: The center of the web.
options.B: The glue on the lines.
options.C: The anchor threads.
options.D: The capture spiral.

ev.t: The whole web is in tension and held in place by anchor threads, which connect the frame to the surrounding vegetation or objects.

note: 第 2 段說整張網靠固定絲（anchor threads）固定在原位，固定絲把外框繫在周圍的植物或物體上；後面也說比較強韌的那種絲用在固定絲上。讓整張網維持在原位的是固定絲，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 capture spiral，捕獵螺旋是用來捕捉並困住獵物的；(B) 照抄 glue，黏液塗在捕獵螺旋的絲上，作用也是黏住獵物；(A) 照抄 center，網的中心是放射絲的起點，原文沒有說網靠中心固定。

stem: According to the passage, which statement is true about the silk threads?

options.A: They are all sticky and extendable.
options.B: They are usually strong enough to last for a day.
options.C: They remove harmful chemicals from insects.
options.D: They are made of rare plants in the environment.

ev.t: the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.

note: 題目問的是網絲（silk threads），答案在第 1 段：網絲必須承受獵物撞擊和風雨的力量，大多數情況下（in most cases）至少要維持一天（for at least a day）。選項把 in most cases 換成 usually，把承受得住、維持一天換成 strong enough to last for a day，所以是 (B)。(A) 的 all 是陷阱：第 2 段說蜘蛛網用了兩種絲，只有捕獵螺旋那一種有彈性、塗了黏液，另一種比較硬，不是全部的絲都會黏、都能拉長；(D) 第 2 段的植物（vegetation）是固定絲繫住的地方，蜘蛛絲是天然的複合材料，原文沒有說是用稀有植物做的；(C) 原文沒有提到去除昆蟲身上的化學物質。

stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Researchers have found an effective way to halt the spread of insect-borne diseases around the world.
options.B: Many people are worried about the effects of genetically modified organisms on the environment.
options.C: It takes time to gain public support for the application of genetic modification to disease control.
options.D: Genetic engineering looks promising in reducing malaria, though there may be unknown consequences.

note: 先看全文怎麼安排：第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，還沒有有效的疫苗；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，讓蚊子無法傳播瘧疾；第 3、4 段說還有兩個挑戰，包括基因改造生物的長期影響還不清楚。主旨要同時說出這個方法有希望，也還有隱憂，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (A)，這個選項照抄第 1 段的 effective：原文只談瘧疾，不是全世界所有由蚊蟲傳播的疾病，而且第 3、4 段說還有很多挑戰，說已經找到有效的方法，說法太過武斷，太過廣泛。(B) 照抄 environment、(C) 照抄 public，環保人士的疑慮和爭取大眾認同，都只是第 4 段的內容，過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following best shows the organization of this passage?

options.A: Introduction → Comparison → Contrast
options.B: Problem → Solution → Potential difficulties
options.C: Proposal → Arguments → Counter-arguments
options.D: Definition → Examples → Tentative conclusions

note: 第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，又沒有有效的疫苗，這是問題（Problem）；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，這是解決方法（Solution）；第 3 段用 Despite this achievement 帶出第一個挑戰，第 4 段用 Another challenge 帶出第二個挑戰，這是可能遇到的困難（Potential difficulties）。所以是 (B)。(A) 全文沒有比較和對照；(C) 原文沒有正反兩方的辯論，第 4 段環保人士的疑慮是挑戰之一；(D) 第 1 段不是在下定義，最後也沒有暫時的結論。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about malaria parasites?

options.A: They are resistant to genetic modification and vaccines.
options.B: They reproduce in the human liver and grow stronger there.
options.C: They can be found in only one gender of a class of mosquitoes.
options.D: They are transmitted to around one million children each year.

ev.t: The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito.

note: 第 1 段說瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性（female）瘧蚊（Anopheles mosquito）攜帶。female 是一種性別（one gender），Anopheles 是蚊子裡的一類（a class of mosquitoes），所以只有一種性別的某一類蚊子身上有瘧疾寄生蟲，是 (C)。(B) 照抄 liver，寄生蟲先到肝臟，接著進入血液，在血液裡繁殖；(D) 照抄 one million，每年大約一百萬人死於瘧疾，其中很多是兒童，不是每年傳給一百萬名兒童；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 resistant，原文說下一代寄生蟲可能會對改造的機制產生抗性，這是還沒發生的情況，沒有疫苗也不表示寄生蟲對疫苗有抗性。

stem: What does “that” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Some malaria parasites escaping from the ecosystems.
options.B: Malaria parasites becoming immune to the engineered bacterium.
options.C: Modified mosquitoes becoming more competitive than the wild ones.
options.D: Transmission of malaria being blocked from mosquitoes to humans.

ev.t: If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it.

note: that 指前一句說的情況：要是有寄生蟲從這個機制漏網，下一代寄生蟲很可能對它產生抗性（become resistant to it）。句中的 it 指 the mechanism，也就是第 2 段說的方法，改造蚊子體內的細菌來殺死寄生蟲。選項把 resistant 換成 immune，把這個機制換成 the engineered bacterium，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 competitive，讓改造蚊子更有競爭力是科學家要達成的目標，如果做到了，不會「從頭來過」；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ecosystems，生態系是環保人士擔心的事情，而且原文說的是寄生蟲從機制中漏網，不是從生態系逃走；(D) 阻斷瘧疾從蚊子傳給人，是第 2 段的成果，也不會讓科學家從頭來過。

stem: Why did Drais invent the running machine?

options.A: To prove his creativity as an inventor.
options.B: To protect the horses from being abused.
options.C: To provide a new gadget for the royal class.
options.D: To give the general public a better means of transportation.

ev.t: to find a muscle-powered replacement for the horses
The machine, he believed, would allow large numbers of people faster movement than walking or riding in a coach.

note: 第 2 段說德萊斯的構想是讓一般大眾受益（big democratic idea）：找一種靠人力的交通工具取代昂貴的馬，讓許多人（large numbers of people）移動得比走路或坐馬車更快。選項換成 give the general public a better means of transportation，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 horses，原文說要取代馬，是因為馬很貴、很會吃，不是為了保護馬不受虐待；(A) 第 1 段說他是很有創意的發明家，但那是作者的介紹，不是他發明滑行車的理由；(C) 原文說的是讓大眾受益，不是替貴族做新玩意兒。

stem: What does “marked the big bang” mean in the second paragraph?

options.A: Gave out huge noise.
options.B: Created serious disturbance.
options.C: Enjoyed wide popularity.
options.D: Represented groundbreaking work.

ev.t: Though not a bike in the modern sense of the word
It was the first vehicle with two wheels placed in line.

note: big bang 原本指宇宙的大霹靂，也就是宇宙的起點；mark 是「標誌著」。這一句用 Though 讓步：雖然滑行車不是現代意義上的自行車，卻標誌著自行車發展的 big bang。下一句接著說，滑行車是第一輛兩個輪子前後排成一直線的車。這是開創性的成就，所以是 (D)。(A) 把 bang 照字面當成巨響；(B) 第 4 段滑行車常撞上行人，那是後來的事，不是這一句的意思；(C) 滑行車在巴黎流行是第 3 段的事，big bang 說的是開創，不是受歡迎。

stem: Which of the following descriptions is true about the running machine?

options.A: It was equipped with cranks and pedals.
options.B: Its wheels and frame were made of iron.
options.C: It had a brake to control the speed of its movement.

ev.t: the steering already resembled a modern handlebar.

note: 第 2 段說滑行車的轉向裝置已經很像（resembled）現代的把手，選項換成 was similar to the handlebar of a modern bike，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 4 段的 cranks and pedals、(C) 照抄 brake，第 4 段說滑行車沒有煞車，也沒有曲柄和踏板（lacked），選項說反了；(B) 照抄 frame，第 2 段說車架和輪子都是木頭做的，不是鐵。

stem: Why did the hobby horse fail to become a common vehicle in the 19th century?

options.A: It was expensive and not durable enough.
options.B: It did not go as fast as people had expected.
options.C: It was hard to control and dangerous to ride on the road.
options.D: It did not receive enough public attention in European cities.

ev.t: They were heavy and difficult to ride.
There were frequent collisions with unsuspecting pedestrians

note: 第 4 段說滑行車很重，也很難騎（difficult to ride），而且沒有煞車，常常撞上行人，安全是問題，所以許多城市禁止使用。選項換成 hard to control and dangerous to ride on the road，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 expensive，昂貴的是馬，滑行車是要取代馬的交通工具；(D) 照抄 European，歐洲城市禁止使用，是因為太危險，不是沒人注意，第 3 段還說滑行車在巴黎很快流行起來；(B) 第 3 段說德萊斯四個小時騎了 60 公里，轟動一時，原文沒有說速度不如預期。

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: A new design in lighting.

note: 題目問哪一個不是 Arnal 團隊的發現。(A) 第 1 段說尖叫的音量變化很快，這就是尖叫和其他聲音不同的地方，是發現；(C) 第 1 段說一般說話的音量變化在 4 到 5 赫茲之間，是發現；(D) 第 2 段說聽到尖叫以後，杏仁核亮了起來，是發現。(B) 和原文矛盾：第 3 段說人工的聲音也常常有粗糙度，鬧鐘、汽車喇叭和火災警報器的粗糙度都很高，可見不是只有人類發得出音量變化大的聲音，所以選 (B)。

stem: What does “it” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: The study.
options.B: Language.
options.C: Roughness.
options.D: The amygdala.

ev.t: roughness isn’t heard when we speak naturally, regardless of the language we use, but it is prevalent in artificial sounds.

note: 這一句用 but 連接兩個對比的部分：粗糙度（roughness）在自然說話時聽不到，但 it 在人工的聲音裡很普遍。前後兩部分講的是同一件事，聽得到或聽不到的是粗糙度，所以 it 指的是 roughness，答案是 (C)。(B) language 是離 it 最近的名詞，但「語言在人工的聲音裡很普遍」說不通；(A) the study 出現在前一句，研究不會在聲音裡；(D) the amygdala 是第 3 段第一句說的大腦恐懼中樞，「杏仁核在人工的聲音裡很普遍」同樣說不通。

stem: Which of the following devices may be improved with the researchers’ findings?

options.A: Smoke detectors.
options.B: Security cameras.
options.C: Electric bug killers.
options.D: Fire extinguishers.

ev.t: One potential application for this research might be to add roughness to alarm sounds to make them more effective
The most aggravating alarm clocks, car horns, and fire alarms possess high degrees of roughness.

note: 這一題答對率只有 40%。判斷步驟：[1] 第 4 段說這項研究可以用在警報聲（alarm sounds）上，加入粗糙度讓警報更有效；[2] 所以要找的是會發出警報聲的裝置；[3] 煙霧偵測器偵測到煙會發出警報，所以是 (A)。最多人選錯的是 (D)，這個選項照抄第 3 段的 fire，火災警報器會發出聲音，滅火器卻是用來滅火，不會發出警報；(B) 監視器錄的是影像；(C) 電蚊燈用來殺蟲，都不靠警報聲。

stem: Why did Tsar Alexander III choose Peter Fabergé to make the first Easter egg?

options.A: Peter Fabergé was the goldsmith for the royal family.
options.B: Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work.
options.C: Tsar Alexander III received an order from Empress Maria.
options.D: Peter Fabergé owned the most famous Russian jewelry house.

ev.t: whose beautiful creations had caught Maria

note: 第 2 段說沙皇向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，因為他美麗的作品（beautiful creations）先前就吸引了（had caught）瑪麗亞的目光，選項換成 Empress Maria was impressed by Peter Fabergé’s work，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 goldsmith，法貝熱是在第一顆彩蛋讓皇后滿意以後，才獲得皇室特約金匠的頭銜；(C) 照抄 order，下訂單的是沙皇，選項說沙皇接到皇后的訂單，說反了；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 famous Russian，法貝熱公司是後來才成為著名的珠寶商，沙皇訂製時，第 2 段說他還是年輕的珠寶師。

stem: What went missing from the first Fabergé egg?

options.A: A golden hen and a ruby egg.
options.B: A golden hen and a golden yolk.
options.C: A ruby egg and a diamond crown.
options.D: A golden yolk and a diamond crown.

ev.t: concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg.
Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.

note: 第 2 段依序說蛋打開來是金蛋黃，蛋黃裡有金母雞，母雞裡藏著鑽石小皇冠（a diamond miniature of the royal crown）和紅寶石小蛋（a tiny ruby egg），接著說最後兩樣驚喜（the last two surprises）已經失傳。最後兩樣就是鑽石皇冠和紅寶石蛋，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 golden hen、(B) 和 (D) 照抄 golden yolk，金母雞和金蛋黃是前面兩樣，沒有失傳。
map: diamond miniature of the royal crown

stem: What does it mean by “Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge” in the third paragraph?

options.A: They repeated their designs over and over.
options.B: They fulfilled the Tsar’s requirements each time.
options.C: They challenged the Tsar’s expectations every year.
options.D: They were faced with unexpected difficulties time and again.

ev.t: The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise.
Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge.

note: 這裡的 meet 不是「遇到」，而是「達成、符合」，meet the challenge 是成功應付挑戰。the challenge 指的是前一句沙皇的要求（The requirements）：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，而且要藏著驚喜；repeatedly 是每年一次又一次。合起來就是法貝熱和繼承人每一次都做到了沙皇的要求，所以是 (B)。(D) 把 meet 當成「遇到」，又把 challenge 當成困難，照字面解釋；(C) 照抄 challenge，挑戰是沙皇給法貝熱的，選項說法貝熱挑戰沙皇，主客顛倒；(A) 照抄 repeated，原文要求每顆彩蛋都獨一無二，不可能重複同樣的設計。

stem: Which of the following statements about the Fabergé eggs is true, according to the passage?

options.A: They were all genuine creations of the jeweler, Peter Fabergé.
options.B: They were created to represent Russian emperors and their dynasty.
options.C: They were made for annual Easter parties in the Russian imperial court.
options.D: They were connected to the last two Russian emperors and their families.

ev.t: for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.
they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.

note: 這一題要把兩段合起來看。第 3 段說法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世做彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止；第 4 段說這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。革命以後俄國就沒有沙皇了，所以這兩位是俄國最後兩位皇帝，彩蛋又是送給皇后等家人的禮物，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Peter Fabergé，第 3 段說彩蛋是他和他的繼承人（his successors）做的，不全是他本人的作品；(C) 照抄 Easter，彩蛋是復活節送給皇后的禮物，原文沒有說是為宮廷的復活節派對做的；(B) 讓人想起俄國最後的皇室，是彩蛋今天的意義，彩蛋當初是沙皇送皇后的禮物，不是為了代表皇帝和王朝而做。

stem: According to the passage, what is “Six Sigma”?

options.A: A digital device to speed up production processes.
options.B: A near-perfect process in business communication.
options.C: A statistical term that measures a company’s budgets and profits.
options.D: A quality measure that detects problems to improve products and services.

ev.t: helps companies focus on developing and delivering near-perfect products and services.
they can systematically figure out how to eliminate the problems

note: 第 1 段說六標準差幫助公司提供近乎完美的產品和服務（products and services），做法是算出生產流程有多少瑕疵，再有系統地找出消除問題（eliminate the problems）的方法，選項換成找出問題、改善產品和服務的品質管理方法，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 statistical term，原文說 sigma 這個字是統計名詞，衡量的是流程離完美多遠，不是預算和利潤；(B) 照抄 near-perfect，近乎完美的是產品和服務，不是商業溝通；(A) 六標準差是一套流程，不是數位裝置。

stem: For Six Sigma to be applied successfully, which of the following are the most crucial factors?

options.A: Customers and suppliers’ needs.
options.B: Tools in statistics and marketing.
options.C: Strong teamwork and proper training.
options.D: Good leadership and sufficient budget.

ev.t: Training and teamwork are essential elements of the Six Sigma methodology.

note: 第 2 段第一句說訓練（Training）和團隊合作（teamwork）是六標準差不可或缺的要素（essential elements），題目的 most crucial factors 就是這一句，所以是 (C)。這一段後面幾句是在說明要訓練什麼：(A) 照抄 customers and suppliers，滿足顧客和供應商的需求，是溝通技巧要達成的事；(B) 照抄 tools，原文說的是測量和改善的工具，沒有提到行銷；(D) 照抄 leader，原文說要訓練組長（team leaders），沒有說領導能力是關鍵，也沒有提到預算。

stem: How are the author’s ideas developed in the last two paragraphs?

options.A: By definition.
options.B: By comparison.
options.C: In time order.
options.D: In space order.

ev.t: Six Sigma was developed in 1986 by Motorola
A few years later
In 1995, Jack Welch
By 2000, Six Sigma was effectively established as an industry in its own right

note: 這一題答對率只有 52%，判斷方法是找出兩段裡的時間詞。第 3 段依序是 1986 年（摩托羅拉發展出六標準差）、A few years later（擴大成一般的績效改善方法）、1995 年（奇異公司導入）、1998 年（省下成本）；第 4 段接著是 By 2000（自成一個產業）。兩段照時間先後說明六標準差的發展，所以是 (C)。(A) 下定義是第 1 段的寫法，第 1 段說明六標準差是什麼；(B) 兩段沒有拿六標準差和別的方法比較；(D) 空間順序是依位置描寫，例如描寫一個地方，這兩段沒有這樣寫。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true regarding Six Sigma?

options.A: It helped Motorola and General Motors to promote sales.
options.B: It requires multi-national efforts to generate satisfactory results.
options.C: It has gained popularity mostly among large telecommunications companies.
options.D: It has become a business model which provides services to organizations worldwide.

ev.t: involving the training, consultancy and implementation of Six Sigma methodology in all sorts of organizations around the world.

note: 第 4 段說到了 2000 年，六標準差已經自成一個產業，在世界各地（around the world）各種組織裡提供訓練、諮詢（consultancy）和實施，選項換成成為一種商業模式，替全世界的組織提供服務，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Motorola，第 3 段的另一家公司是奇異公司（General Electrics），不是通用汽車（General Motors），而且原文說的是省下成本，不是促進銷售；(B) 照抄 multi-national，跨國企業只是採用六標準差的組織之一；(C) 照抄 telecommunications，電信公司只是發展出六標準差的摩托羅拉，第 4 段說採用的組織從政府、監獄到銀行都有。

stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Bottlenose dolphins show strong ties to their family members.
options.B: Bottlenose dolphins recognize their friends’ voices in the wild.
options.C: Bottlenose dolphins produce whistles that distinguish themselves.
options.D: Bottlenose dolphins demonstrate a unique type of animal communication.

note: 這一題答對率只有 44%，三個錯誤選項都只講到全文的一部分。第 1 段說科學家相信海豚會叫彼此的名字；第 2、3 段說明海豚會模仿親近同伴的哨聲來呼喚對方；第 4 段說這種用法和人類語言相似，和鳥類不同；第 5 段說這是自然界少見的溝通層次（a level of communication rarely found in nature）。全文講的是海豚獨特的溝通方式，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 whistles，海豚發出自己的專屬哨聲只是一半，重點是模仿別的海豚的哨聲來呼叫對方，過於狹隘；(A) 母海豚和小海豚只是第 3 段說的情形之一，過於狹隘；(B) 第 3 段的研究是把海豚分開放在網子裡，而且說野外偶然相遇的海豚不會這樣做，選項只講認出朋友的聲音，過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about Wells’s research team?

options.A: Their data were collected over two decades.
options.B: They recorded the calls of dolphins and birds.
options.C: Their major research base was in Mexico.
options.D: They trained 250 wild dolphins for observation.

ev.t: made around Florida’s Sarasota Bay from 1984 to 2009

note: 第 3 段說錄音是 1984 年到 2009 年（from 1984 to 2009）錄下的，前後 25 年，超過二十年，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 birds，鳥類只是拿來和海豚比較，研究團隊錄的是海豚的聲音；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Mexico，墨西哥灣只是開頭請讀者想像的場景，研究地點在佛羅里達州的薩拉索塔灣；(D) 照抄 250 wild，研究人員是聽 250 隻野生海豚的錄音，沒有訓練牠們。

stem: What does “this” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Recording messages.
options.B: Conducting research.
options.C: Behavior learning.
options.D: Whistle copying.

ev.t: dolphins familiar with each other would mimic the whistle of another in that group when they were separated.
Most of this took place among mothers and calves

note: Most of this 的前一句說，熟識的海豚分開時，會模仿另一隻海豚的哨聲（mimic the whistle）。大多發生在母海豚和小海豚之間的，就是這種模仿哨聲的行為，這一段最後一句也用 Whistle copying of this sort 再說一次，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 recordings，錄音是研究人員做的事；(B) 照抄 research，研究也是研究人員做的事，不會發生在海豚母子之間；(C) 原文沒有談到學習行為。

stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Birds may use their calls to claim territory.
options.B: Male dolphins whistle when fighting for mates.
options.C: Dolphins make harsh squeaks when hunting for food.
options.D: Both dolphins and birds tend to mimic their enemies’ whistles.

ev.t: the maintenance of social bonds appears to be more important than the immediate defense of resources.
which tend to address one another in a more

note: 這一題答對率只有 41%，要把第 4 段的兩句連起來推。判斷步驟：[1] 第 4 段說海豚和人類一樣，用模仿聲音來維繫社會關係，這比立即保衛資源（defense of resources）重要；[2] 接著說鳥類和海豚不同，比較會在具有攻擊性的情境下呼叫彼此；[3] 和「維繫關係」相反的就是「保衛資源」，鳥類的叫聲比較可能用來保衛資源，地盤就是一種資源，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 males，原文說關係密切的雄海豚之間會模仿哨聲，是表示親近，不是爭奪配偶；(C) 照抄第 5 段的 squeaks，那是用來表明身分、呼叫朋友的聲音，原文沒有提到獵食；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 mimic，海豚模仿的是親近、想再見面的同伴，不是敵人。

stem: How is the landscape of the Goreme National Park formed?

options.A: It is the effect of erosions of volcanic rocks by wind and water.
options.B: It is the outcome of cumulative ash and lava from volcanoes.
options.C: It is the creation of some mysterious forces from the moon.
options.D: It is the result of rock cutting by the Byzantine Christians.

ev.t: Over the centuries the wind and rain worked their magic on this land, carving out spectacular gorges
the wind and rain start to cut away the cone until it, too, collapses.

note: 這一題答對率只有 46%，要分清楚「土地怎麼來的」和「地形怎麼刻出來的」。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說火山噴出的火山灰和熔岩形成了卡帕多奇亞地區，這是岩石的來源；[2] 接著說風和雨（the wind and rain）在這片土地上切出峽谷，留下岩柱，後來又繼續削蝕錐體；[3] 題目問的是地形（landscape）怎麼形成的，刻出地形的是風雨對火山岩的侵蝕，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 ash and lava，火山灰和熔岩只是材料，還要經過風雨侵蝕才變成今天的地形；(C) 照抄 moonscape 的 moon，月面景觀是形容景觀像月球表面，不是月球的力量造成的；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 Byzantine Christians，基督徒鑿的是教堂和村莊，不是整片地形。

stem: Which of the following descriptions of the “fairy chimneys” is true?

options.A: They are almost identical in size and shape.
options.B: They have mushrooms growing on the top.
options.C: They are formed by rocks of different hardness.
options.D: They have strong bottoms to support their 40-meter height.

ev.t: The top stone is the hardest part of each formation and protects the softer rock underneath from erosion.

note: 這一題答對率只有 49%。第 2 段說頂端的石頭最硬（the hardest），保護下方比較軟（softer）的岩石，可見仙女煙囪是由軟硬不同的岩石構成的，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 shape，原文說仙女煙囪的形狀和大小非常多樣，不是幾乎一樣；(B) 照抄 mushrooms，原文說仙女煙囪的外形像杏鮑菇，不是上面長了香菇；(D) 照抄 40，原文說下方的岩石比較軟，風雨會把錐體削蝕到倒塌，底部並不堅固。

stem: Which of the following has NOT been a function served by the carved rocks in the Goreme National Park?

options.A: Refuge.
options.B: Gallery.
options.C: Residence.
options.D: Place of worship.

ev.t: They carved thousands of cave churches, chapels, and monasteries out of rock.
in an effort to hide from the Romans
many of these villages are still inhabited

note: 這一題答對率只有 42%，要逐一核對鑿出來的岩石有過哪些用途。第 3 段說拜占庭的基督徒在岩石上鑿出教堂、禮拜堂和修道院，是 (D) 做禮拜的地方；鑿出地下村莊來躲避羅馬人和穆斯林，是 (A) 避難所；這些村莊到今天還有人居住，是 (C) 住所。最容易選錯的是 (B)：原文雖然說教堂裡有美麗的壁畫，但壁畫是教堂的裝飾，鑿出來的岩石並沒有當作展示畫作的藝廊，所以選 (B)。

stem: Which of the following sentences best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Goreme is a wonder where nature meets man.
options.B: Goreme is a representation of ancient Turkish life.
options.C: Goreme is a living example of the power of nature.
options.D: Goreme is an attraction that mixes the new and the old.

note: 這一題答對率只有 28%，是這一批最低的，判斷的方法是找出段落之間的轉折。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段講自然：火山和風雨造出峽谷和仙女煙囪；[2] 第 3 段第一句用 But 轉折，說這座公園不只有壯觀的風景，人類（Humans, too）也在這裡留下印記，接著講拜占庭基督徒鑿的教堂和地下村莊；[3] 第 1 段的三樣東西也是自然和人文都有：高聳的岩石、波紋地形是自然，地下城市是人文。全文是自然加上人文，所以是 (A)。(C) 只講第 2 段的自然力量，過於狹隘；(B) 只講第 3 段的人文，過於狹隘，而且在這裡生活的是拜占庭的基督徒，原文沒有說是古代土耳其人，ancient 是第 2 段形容火山的字；(D) 原文沒有拿新的和舊的東西做對比，偏離主題。

stem: What was the purpose of building the Brooklyn Bridge?

options.D: To provide faster and safer transportation than boats.

ev.t: Before that, the only transportation was by ferries, which were slow and could be dangerous in winter.

note: 第 1 段說大橋提供了曼哈頓島和布魯克林之間的第一條交通幹道，在那之前只能搭渡輪（ferries），渡輪速度慢（slow），冬天還可能有危險（dangerous）。建橋是為了提供比船更快、更安全的交通，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 model，大橋成為後來吊橋的典範，是建好以後的結果，不是建橋的目的；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 Civil War，南北戰爭反而讓建橋計畫停了下來；(A) 原文說這是第一條交通幹道，之前沒有橋，談不上取代舊橋。

stem: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “deflected” in the second paragraph?

options.A: Blocked.
options.B: Detected.
options.C: Engaged.
options.D: Indicated.

ev.t: but the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861 deflected all consideration of the project.
When the war ended in 1865, the bridge became an important issue once more.

note: deflect 原來的意思是「使轉向」，例如球打到東西以後彈開、改變方向。這一句用 but 轉折：19 世紀初就有人討論建橋，但南北戰爭爆發，deflected 了所有對這項計畫的考慮；下一句又說戰爭結束以後，建橋再度（once more）成為重要議題。可見戰爭期間大家的注意力轉到別處，計畫停了下來，所以是 (A) 擋下來了。(C) 投入、(D) 指出，都和下一句的 once more 接不上；(B) 察覺，和 consideration 放在一起意思說不通。

stem: Which of the following is true about the Brooklyn Bridge?

options.A: It was built in 1865.
options.B: It is shorter than originally planned.
options.C: It was first proposed after the Civil War.
options.D: It was built by the New York Bridge Company.

ev.t: In 1867, the New York State legislature passed an act incorporating the New York Bridge Company for the purpose of constructing and maintaining a bridge

note: 第 2 段說 1867 年紐約州議會通過法案，成立紐約橋梁公司（the New York Bridge Company），目的是建造（constructing）並維護這座橋，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 1865，那是南北戰爭結束的年份，大橋 1883 年才啟用；(C) 照抄 Civil War，19 世紀初就有人討論建橋，比南北戰爭早；(B) 第 4 段說實際建成的橋比原來提議的 1,500 英尺更長，選項說反了。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following correctly describes John Augustus Roebling?

options.A: He participated in the Civil War and was seriously wounded.
options.B: He was chosen to design the bridge because of his radical views.
options.C: He was the first person to propose the construction of the bridge.
options.D: He moved to America because he was discriminated against in his home country.

ev.t: He emigrated to America in 1830 to escape political discrimination.

note: 第 3 段說 Roebling 1830 年移民到美國（emigrated to America），為的是逃避政治歧視（political discrimination），選項換成他為了躲開祖國的歧視而搬到美國，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 radical views，激進的思想是他學生時代在德國的事，原文沒有說他因此獲選設計大橋；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 Civil War，原文沒有說他參加南北戰爭；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 proposed，他提議的是橋的設計，19 世紀初就有人討論建橋了。

stem: What is the best title of this passage?

options.A: Heart Diseases and Their Causes
options.B: The Power of Social Connection
options.C: Differences in Japanese Americans
options.D: The Sense of Belonging vs. Isolation

note: 這一題答對率只有 52%，判斷的方法是先找出全文的結論在哪一段。第 1 段提出問題：日本男性大多抽菸，心臟病發生率卻最低，是什麼在保護他們？第 2、3 段說明研究結果：抽菸、飲食都無法解釋差異，有關的是社會型態；第 4 段說出結論：和社會團體建立連結，是決定健康的關鍵。全文講的是社會連結的力量，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄 heart disease，心臟病只是研究用來衡量健康的指標，文章並沒有介紹心臟病的各種原因，太過廣泛；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 Japanese Americans，日裔美國人之間的差異只是研究的發現，過於狹隘；(D) 用 vs. 把歸屬感和孤立當成兩方來比較，卻沒有說到兩者對健康的影響，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following is a finding of the two American professors’ study?

options.A: Many Japanese men that lived up to 100 years were smokers.
options.B: Those who often ate hamburgers and fries were more likely to fall sick.
options.C: Japanese immigrants to America usually formed a tight-knit community.
options.D: Westernized social life was related to the heart-attack rate of Japanese Americans.

ev.t: However, the kind of society they had created for themselves in their new home country was.
But those who had adopted the more isolated Western lifestyle increased their heart-attack incidence by three to five times.

note: 這一題答對率只有 54%，三個錯誤選項都照抄原文，但說的不是兩位教授的研究發現。第 3 段說，和心臟病增加有關的，是他們在新國家建立的社會型態；採用西方比較孤立的生活方式（Western lifestyle）的人，心臟病發作的比率增加三到五倍，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 100 years，日本人長壽、大多數男性抽菸是研究之前就知道的現象，原文也沒有說活到 100 歲的人大多抽菸；(B) 照抄 hamburgers and fries，第 3 段說飲食變化和心臟病增加無關；(C) 照抄 tight-knit，只有最傳統的那一群維持緊密的社群，原文沒有說日本移民通常都這樣。

stem: Which of the following is an example of “something bigger” in the last paragraph?

options.A: A family.
options.B: A stadium.
options.C: The universe.
options.D: The digital world.

ev.t: We need to feel part of something bigger to thrive.
We need to belong, not online, but in the real world of hugs, handshakes, and pats on the back.

note: 這一題答對率只有 45%，something bigger 不能照字面當成「體積更大的東西」。判斷步驟：[1] 這一段開頭說人需要和社會團體（a social group）建立連結；[2] something bigger 是比自己這個人更大的「群體」，就是前面說的社會團體；[3] 下一句又說這種歸屬感要在真實世界的擁抱、握手、拍肩裡，家人正是這樣的群體，所以是 (A)。(B) 體育場、(C) 宇宙，都是照字面把 bigger 解釋成體積大；(D) 照抄 world，原文說的是 real world，並且特別說歸屬感不是在網路上（not online），數位世界剛好相反。

stem: What is the ratio of heart disease between Japanese living in Japan and Japanese Americans in Hawaii?

options.B: 1 to 5
options.C: 3 to 5

ev.t: It was found that the rate of heart disease among Japanese men increased five times in California and about half of that for those in Hawaii.

note: 這一題答對率只有 54%，要自己算。步驟：[1] 以住在日本的那一組為 1；[2] 第 2 段說移民到加州的心臟病發生率增加為五倍（five times），也就是 5；[3] 移民到夏威夷的，大約是加州的一半（about half of that），5 的一半是 2.5；[4] 日本和夏威夷的比例是 1 比 2.5，所以是 (A)。(B) 1 比 5 是日本和加州的比例；(C) 3 到 5 出自第 3 段的 three to five times，那是採用西方生活方式的人心臟病發作增加的倍數，不是夏威夷那一組；(D) 1.5 比 5 在文章裡找不到依據，以住在日本的一組為 1，夏威夷是 2.5、加州是 5，沒有哪兩組的比例是 1.5 比 5。

stem: What is the purpose of this article?

options.A: To introduce a new currency.
options.B: To prove the value of a young economy.
options.C: To explore ways to do online transactions.
options.D: To explain how to build up a business network.

note: 第 1 段說明比特幣是什麼、怎麼運作；第 2、3 段說交易無法撤銷、交易紀錄公開；第 4 段提醒價格不穩定，不要拿來存錢；第 5 段說比特幣還在發展，未來無法預測。全文在介紹比特幣這種新貨幣，以及使用時要注意的事，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 young economy，經濟還很年輕是價格不穩定的原因，文章是在提醒風險，不是證明它的價值，偏離主題；(C) 網路交易的方式很多，文章只談比特幣，太過廣泛；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 network，原文的網路指的是比特幣的運作系統，文章沒有談怎麼建立商業人脈，偏離主題。

stem: Why is the value of Bitcoin not stable?

options.A: Because its use is illegal.
options.B: Because it is not a valid investment.
options.C: Because it is still developing.
options.D: Because its circulation is limited to the youth.

ev.t: due to its young economy, novel nature, and sometimes illiquid markets.
Bitcoin is an experimental new currency that is in active development.

note: 第 4 段說比特幣的價格可能短時間內漲跌，原因是它的經濟還很年輕、性質很新；第 5 段說比特幣是仍在積極發展（in active development）的實驗性貨幣。還在發展中，所以價值不穩定，答案是 (C)。(D) 的 youth 和第 4 段的 young 看起來相關，但 young economy 是說比特幣的經濟剛起步，不是說只有年輕人在用；(A) 原文沒有說比特幣違法；(B) 原文說比特幣是高風險的資產，沒有說它不是有效的投資。

stem: Which of the following is true about Bitcoin?

options.A: Bitcoin addresses are known only to their owners.
options.B: Once a transaction is made, the Bitcoin cannot be refunded.
options.C: Bitcoin user’s identity is always open to the general public.
options.D: When a payment is received, the Bitcoin can be turned into local currency.

ev.t: If you receive payments with Bitcoin, many service providers can convert them to your local currency.

note: 第 4 段最後一句說，收到比特幣付款，許多服務業者可以替你換成（convert）本國的貨幣（local currency），所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 address，原文說任何人都看得到任何比特幣地址的餘額和交易；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 refunded，交易無法撤銷，但收款人可以退款；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 identity，使用者的身分在揭露資訊以前沒有人知道，選項說反了。

stem: What advice would the author give to those who are interested in keeping money in Bitcoin?

options.A: Better late than never.
options.B: Look before you leap.
options.C: Make hay while the sun shines.
options.D: No pain, no gain.

ev.t: keeping your savings with Bitcoin is not recommended at this point.
you should never store money that you cannot afford to lose with Bitcoin.

note: 第 4 段說目前不建議用比特幣存放儲蓄，輸不起的錢絕對不要放進去；第 5 段又說比特幣的未來沒有人能預測。作者是要想用比特幣存錢的人先想清楚風險，Look before you leap 是「三思而後行」，所以是 (B)。(A) Better late than never 是「晚做總比不做好」，(C) Make hay while the sun shines 是「打鐵趁熱」，(D) No pain, no gain 是「不勞則無獲」，這三句都是鼓勵人趕快去做，和作者提醒風險的意思相反。

stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Researchers have found an effective way to halt the spread of insect-borne diseases around the world.
options.B: Many people are worried about the effects of genetically modified organisms on the environment.
options.C: It takes time to gain public support for the application of genetic modification to disease control.
options.D: Genetic engineering looks promising in reducing malaria, though there may be unknown consequences.

note: 先看全文怎麼安排：第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，還沒有有效的疫苗；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，讓蚊子無法傳播瘧疾；第 3、4 段說還有兩個挑戰，包括基因改造生物的長期影響還不清楚。主旨要同時說出這個方法有希望，也還有隱憂，所以是 (D)。最容易選錯的是 (A)，這個選項照抄第 1 段的 effective：原文只談瘧疾，不是全世界所有由蚊蟲傳播的疾病，而且第 3、4 段說還有很多挑戰，說已經找到有效的方法，說法太過武斷，太過廣泛。(B) 照抄 environment、(C) 照抄 public，環保人士的疑慮和爭取大眾認同，都只是第 4 段的內容，過於狹隘。

stem: Which of the following best shows the organization of this passage?

options.A: Introduction → Comparison → Contrast
options.B: Problem → Solution → Potential difficulties
options.C: Proposal → Arguments → Counter-arguments
options.D: Definition → Examples → Tentative conclusions

note: 第 1 段說瘧疾每年造成大約一百萬人死亡，又沒有有效的疫苗，這是問題（Problem）；第 2 段說科學家改造蚊子體內的細菌，殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，這是解決方法（Solution）；第 3 段用 Despite this achievement 帶出第一個挑戰，第 4 段用 Another challenge 帶出第二個挑戰，這是可能遇到的困難（Potential difficulties）。所以是 (B)。(A) 全文沒有比較和對照；(C) 原文沒有正反兩方的辯論，第 4 段環保人士的疑慮是挑戰之一；(D) 第 1 段不是在下定義，最後也沒有暫時的結論。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about malaria parasites?

options.A: They are resistant to genetic modification and vaccines.
options.B: They reproduce in the human liver and grow stronger there.
options.C: They can be found in only one gender of a class of mosquitoes.
options.D: They are transmitted to around one million children each year.

ev.t: The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito.

note: 第 1 段說瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性（female）瘧蚊（Anopheles mosquito）攜帶。female 是一種性別（one gender），Anopheles 是蚊子裡的一類（a class of mosquitoes），所以只有一種性別的某一類蚊子身上有瘧疾寄生蟲，是 (C)。(B) 照抄 liver，寄生蟲先到肝臟，接著進入血液，在血液裡繁殖；(D) 照抄 one million，每年大約一百萬人死於瘧疾，其中很多是兒童，不是每年傳給一百萬名兒童；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 resistant，原文說下一代寄生蟲可能會對改造的機制產生抗性，這是還沒發生的情況，沒有疫苗也不表示寄生蟲對疫苗有抗性。

stem: What does “that” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.A: Some malaria parasites escaping from the ecosystems.
options.B: Malaria parasites becoming immune to the engineered bacterium.
options.C: Modified mosquitoes becoming more competitive than the wild ones.
options.D: Transmission of malaria being blocked from mosquitoes to humans.

ev.t: If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it.

note: that 指前一句說的情況：要是有寄生蟲從這個機制漏網，下一代寄生蟲很可能對它產生抗性（become resistant to it）。句中的 it 指 the mechanism，也就是第 2 段說的方法，改造蚊子體內的細菌來殺死寄生蟲。選項把 resistant 換成 immune，把這個機制換成 the engineered bacterium，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 competitive，讓改造蚊子更有競爭力是科學家要達成的目標，如果做到了，不會「從頭來過」；(A) 照抄第 4 段的 ecosystems，生態系是環保人士擔心的事情，而且原文說的是寄生蟲從機制中漏網，不是從生態系逃走；(D) 阻斷瘧疾從蚊子傳給人，是第 2 段的成果，也不會讓科學家從頭來過。

stem: Which of the following titles best describes the passage?

options.A: The Economic Value of English Oak.
options.B: How British Squirrels Survive Winters.
options.C: English Oak: What Do We Know about It?
options.D: A Comparison between English Oak and Steel.

note: 第 1 段介紹英國橡木這種木材：堅硬、耐用、構造特別；第 2 段介紹英國橡樹這種樹：葉子、高度、壽命、種子，以及養活的昆蟲。兩段合起來，是在介紹我們對英國橡樹知道些什麼，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 squirrels，松鼠把橡實埋起來過冬，只是說明橡實怎麼長成新樹，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 steel，橡木的強度比鋼強只是第 1 段的一句，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有談橡樹能賺多少錢，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following does “Those” in the second paragraph refer to?

options.A: Acorns.
options.B: Leaves.
options.C: Oak trees.
options.D: Squirrels and jays.

ev.t: Acorns are the favorite food of squirrels and jays who bury them to store them for the winter.
Those that are forgotten survive to form new trees.

note: 前一句說松鼠和松鴉把橡實（Acorns）埋起來，存著過冬；接著說 Those that are forgotten survive to form new trees。牠們會忘記、又能長成新樹的，是埋在土裡的橡實，所以是 (A)。(D) 松鼠和松鴉是忘記的一方，不會長成樹；(C) 橡樹是橡實長出來的結果，不是忘記的東西；(B) 葉子在這一段的第二句，和埋起來過冬無關。

stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: English oak used in old buildings is not as durable as steel.
options.B: Oak timber can be made into thousands of drinking straws.
options.C: In England, oak trees support more insects than other trees.
options.D: English oak is rare due to its heavy use in the construction industry.

ev.t: Of all British trees, the oak sustains the largest number of insects, over 500 species.

note: 第 2 段說在英國所有的樹木中，橡樹養活（sustains）的昆蟲種類最多，選項換成在英國，橡樹養活的昆蟲比其他樹多，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 durable，原文說橡木耐久的強度比鋼還強，選項說反了；(B) 照抄 drinking straws，吸管是用來比喻橡木的管狀細胞，不是拿橡木做吸管；(D) 第 2 段說橡樹是英國最常見的樹木之一，並不稀少。

stem: Which of the following questions can NOT be answered by the passage?

options.A: How many species of insects does English oak support?
options.B: How does English oak live for 1,000 years or more?
options.C: What does English oak provide for jays in winter?
options.D: Why do buildings made of English oak survive for centuries?

ev.t: over 500 species.
Acorns are the favorite food of squirrels and jays
this complex architecture gives the wood its remarkable structural properties
can live for 1,000 years or more.

note: 題目問哪一個問題文章回答不了。(A) 第 2 段說橡樹養活的昆蟲超過 500 種，回答得了；(C) 第 2 段說橡實是松鴉最愛吃的食物，牠們埋起來過冬，回答得了；(D) 第 1 段說管狀細胞的複雜構造讓橡木耐久，所以橡木建築能用好幾百年，回答得了。(B) 第 2 段只說橡樹可以活一千年以上，沒有說明為什麼能活這麼久，所以選 (B)。

stem: According to the passage, when may the “lipstick effect” occur?

options.A: When people’s budgets are tight.
options.B: When the economy is recovering.
options.C: When women want to look attractive.
options.D: When cosmetic companies put lipstick on sale.

ev.t: when they feel their budgets are squeezed
during an economic recession

note: 第 1 段說口紅效應發生在經濟衰退期間（during an economic recession）；第 2 段說女性覺得預算吃緊（budgets are squeezed）的時候，會買口紅讓自己開心，選項換成 budgets are tight，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 economy，口紅效應出現在經濟低迷的時候，不是經濟復甦的時候；(D) 照抄 sales，原文說的是化妝品的銷量（sales），不是化妝品公司打折（on sale）；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 women，女性想變漂亮不是口紅效應的成因，重點是預算吃緊時買小東西讓自己開心。

stem: Why are people unhappy when lipstick is selling well?

options.A: Because women are too wasteful.
options.B: Because it affects industrial production.
options.C: Because it is a sign of an economic recession.
options.D: Because Estée Lauder is making too much money.
