options.C: Dogs have a better sense of smell than pigs.
options.D: Dogs are less likely to get excited than pigs.

ev.t: The use of pigs is risky, though, because of their natural tendency to eat any remotely edible thing.
they willingly exchange their truffle for a piece of bread and a pat on the head.

note: 第 2 段說用豬有風險，因為豬天生什麼東西能吃就吃（eat any remotely edible thing），挖到的松露可能直接吃掉；狗則願意用松露換一塊麵包。兩句合起來，就是狗通常不會吃掉找到的松露，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 smell，原文說母豬對松露的氣味特別敏感，沒有說狗的嗅覺比豬好；(A) 照抄 dig，原文說人們訓練狗往下挖，沒有比較狗和豬的腳掌；(D) 原文沒有提到哪一種動物比較容易興奮。

stem: What is the best way to enjoy truffles as a delicacy?

options.A: Eating them cooked with pork.
options.B: Eating them uncooked with bland oil.
options.C: Eating them fresh right after being collected.
options.D: Eating them after being refrigerated.

ev.t: you must eat fresh, uncooked specimens shortly after they have been harvested.

note: 第 3 段說想享受松露的風味，一定要在採集後不久（shortly after they have been harvested）就吃新鮮（fresh）的生松露，選項把 harvested 換成 collected，所以是 (C)。(B) 和 (D) 都照抄同一段後面的字：bland oil 和 refrigerator 是保存松露的方法，原文接著說風味會隨著時間迅速變淡，所以保存起來的松露不是最好的吃法；(A) 原文說要吃生的，沒有提到和豬肉一起煮。
map: shortly after they have been harvested

stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Truffles are roots of some old trees.
options.B: Truffles can be found only by dogs and pigs.
options.C: Truffles send out a strong odor when they mature.
options.D: Truffles cannot be collected at the same place repeatedly.

ev.t: which are able to detect the strong smell of mature truffles underneath the surface of the ground.

note: 第 2 段說母豬和松露犬聞得到地面下成熟（mature）松露的強烈氣味（strong smell），也就是說松露成熟時會散發強烈的氣味，選項把 smell 換成 odor，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 roots，原文說松露和樹根共生，松露本身是蕈類，不是樹根；(B) 照抄 dogs，同一段說有些商人看到松露蠅盤旋，就自己動手挖，所以不是只有狗和豬找得到；(D) 照抄 collected，原文說找到一個地點以後，往後幾年都可以在那裡採集，選項說反了。

stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Truffles sold in glass jars are tasteless.
options.B: Truffles taste like fruit when eaten fresh.
options.C: Truffles are only used for cooking nowadays.
options.D: Truffles are expensive because they are difficult to find.

ev.t: They are among the most expensive of the world’s natural foods
This is why they are difficult to find.

note: 第 1 段先說松露是全世界最昂貴的天然食物之一，接著說松露長在地底下，所以很難找到（difficult to find）。原文沒有直接說「因為難找所以貴」，要把同一段的兩件事連起來，推得出松露貴是因為難找，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 glass jars，原文說裝進玻璃罐冷藏是保存的方法，沒有說罐裝松露沒有味道；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 fruit，fruiting bodies 是蕈類的子實體，和水果的味道無關；(C) 第 1 段說歐洲人把松露當珍饈，也當藥材，原文沒有說現在只用來做菜。

stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: The success of animal experiments should be ensured.
options.B: Ban on the use of animals in the lab should be enforced.
options.C: Greater efforts need to be taken to reduce the number of lab animals.
options.D: Scientists should be required to share their research results with each other.

note: 第 1 段說動物實驗仍有必要，但每年用掉 5,000 萬到 1 億隻動物；第 2 段說各國實際用的動物數量；第 3 段說歐洲正在限制實驗動物的數量，推薦替代方法和公開研究結果；第 4 段說歐洲的新措施應該能減少實驗用的動物。全文要說的是應該更努力減少實驗動物的數量，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 3 段的 research results，分享研究結果只是減少動物數量的方法之一，過於狹隘；(B) 第 4 段說動物實驗需要繼續下去，作者沒有主張禁止，偏離主題；(A) 文章沒有談怎麼確保實驗成功，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about animals used in the lab?

options.A: America uses only about 1.1 million lab animals per year.
options.B: Europe does not use mice and rats as lab animals at all.
options.C: Britain does not use as many lab animals as China does.
options.D: Japan has limited data on the number of lab animals used each year.

ev.t: Japan and China have even less comprehensive data than America.

note: 這一題答對率只有 46%，錯誤選項都照抄第 2 段的字，要逐項回原文核對。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段最後一句說日本和中國的資料比美國還不完整（less comprehensive data），選項換成日本每年使用的實驗動物數量資料有限，所以是 (D)；[2] (A) 照抄 1.1 million，但原文接著說這個數字會讓人誤解，因為美國沒有把小鼠和大鼠算進去，實際的數字要高得多，選項加了 only，和原文相反；[3] (B) 照抄 mice and rats，原文說歐洲用的動物大多是小鼠和大鼠，選項說反了；[4] (C) 照抄 China，原文沒有提到英國，也沒有比較英國和中國。

stem: Which of the following is mentioned as an alternative to replace animal experiments?

options.A: Statistical studies.
options.B: Computer models.
options.C: DNA planted in animals.
options.D: Tissue from dead animals.

ev.t: such as using human tissue or computer models

note: 第 3 段說動物實驗的替代方法，例如使用人體組織或電腦模型（computer models），所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 tissue，原文說的是人體組織（human tissue），選項換成死去動物的組織，對的字放錯了對象；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 statistics，那是美國官方統計實驗動物的數量，不是替代方法；(C) 原文沒有提到把 DNA 植入動物。

stem: What usually happens to unsuccessful animal experiments?

options.A: They are not revealed to the public.
options.B: They are made into teaching materials.
options.C: They are collected for future publication.
options.D: They are not removed from the research topic list.

ev.t: If their findings do not fit the hypothesis being tested, the work never sees the light of day.

note: 第 3 段說目前科學家常常只分享成功的實驗結果，如果研究發現不符合要驗證的假設，這項研究就永遠不會公開（never sees the light of day）。see the light of day 是首次出現、公之於世的意思，選項換成不會向大眾公開，所以是 (A)。(B) 做成教材、(C) 收集起來日後出版、(D) 不從研究題目清單上移除，原文都沒有提到；原文接著說這種做法會讓失敗的實驗不斷重複，可見失敗的結果並沒有公開。
map: never sees the light of day

stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: The food network in nature.
options.B: The construction of orb webs.
options.C: The network of geometrical studies.
options.D: The environmental challenges for spider webs.

note: 第 1 段說圓網是最美、結構最有秩序的蜘蛛網，並說明網的功能；第 2 段介紹圓網的兩大特點：幾何結構和建造的材料。全文講的是圓網怎麼構成，所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 environmental，網要承受風雨，只是第 1 段說明網絲需要多強韌，過於狹隘；(A) 蜘蛛網的功能是捕捉獵物，但全文沒有談自然界的食物網，偏離主題；(C) 第 2 段的幾何結構是在描述網的形狀，不是談幾何學的研究，偏離主題。

stem: What does the word “so” in the first paragraph refer to?

options.A: To catch and keep small creatures.
options.B: To find a good material for the web.
options.C: To observe the behavior patterns of spiders.
options.D: To present a fantastic architecture by animals.

ev.t: The main function of the web is to intercept and hold flying prey

note: In order to do so 的 do so 指的是前一句說的事：蜘蛛網的主要功能是攔住並困住（intercept and hold）蒼蠅、蜜蜂等飛行的獵物，讓蜘蛛有時間抓住。選項把飛行的獵物換成 small creatures，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 architecture，動物建築是第 1 段第一句的開場；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 material，網的材料是後面才談的特點；(C) 原文沒有提到觀察蜘蛛的行為。

stem: Which part of the web is used for supporting the web itself?

options.A: The center of the web.
options.B: The glue on the lines.
options.C: The anchor threads.
options.D: The capture spiral.

ev.t: The whole web is in tension and held in place by anchor threads, which connect the frame to the surrounding vegetation or objects.

note: 第 2 段說整張網靠固定絲（anchor threads）固定在原位，固定絲把外框繫在周圍的植物或物體上；後面也說比較強韌的那種絲用在固定絲上。讓整張網維持在原位的是固定絲，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄 capture spiral，捕獵螺旋是用來捕捉並困住獵物的；(B) 照抄 glue，黏液塗在捕獵螺旋的絲上，作用也是黏住獵物；(A) 照抄 center，網的中心是放射絲的起點，原文沒有說網靠中心固定。

stem: According to the passage, which statement is true about the silk threads?

options.A: They are all sticky and extendable.
options.B: They are usually strong enough to last for a day.
options.C: They remove harmful chemicals from insects.
options.D: They are made of rare plants in the environment.

ev.t: the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.

note: 題目問的是網絲（silk threads），答案在第 1 段：網絲必須承受獵物撞擊和風雨的力量，大多數情況下（in most cases）至少要維持一天（for at least a day）。選項把 in most cases 換成 usually，把承受得住、維持一天換成 strong enough to last for a day，所以是 (B)。(A) 的 all 是陷阱：第 2 段說蜘蛛網用了兩種絲，只有捕獵螺旋那一種有彈性、塗了黏液，另一種比較硬，不是全部的絲都會黏、都能拉長；(D) 第 2 段的植物（vegetation）是固定絲繫住的地方，蜘蛛絲是天然的複合材料，原文沒有說是用稀有植物做的；(C) 原文沒有提到去除昆蟲身上的化學物質。

stem: In which country did the modern practice of granting doctoral degrees start?

options.A: France.
options.B: Germany.
options.C: Canada.
options.D: The U.S.

ev.t: The doctorate of philosophy as it exists today originated at Humboldt University.
The German practice was later adopted by American and Canadian universities

note: 這一題答對率只有 39%，題目問現代授予博士學位的做法從哪個國家開始，原文沒有直接寫國名。判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說第一個哲學博士學位 1150 年在巴黎頒發，但接著用 but 說這個學位到 19 世紀初才取得現代的地位，所以巴黎頒發的不是現代的做法，(A) 法國排除；[2] 下一句說現今的博士學位起源於洪堡大學（Humboldt University），再下一句把這套做法稱為 The German practice，可見洪堡大學在德國；[3] 美國和加拿大的大學是後來（later）採用這套做法，(C)、(D) 排除。所以是 (B)。

stem: Which of the following words is closest in meaning to “churned out” in the second paragraph?

options.A: Failed.
options.B: Warned.
options.C: Demanded.
options.D: Produced.

ev.t: Even Japan, where the number of young people is shrinking, has churned out about 46% more PhDs.

note: churn out 是大量產出、快速生產的意思。這一句前面一路說各國博士人數增加，Other countries are catching up，接著用 Even 說連年輕人口減少的日本，博士也多了大約 46%，所以 churned out 是產出，是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 3 段的 warn，提出警告的是研究人員；(C) 照抄第 3 段的 demand，原文說博士的供給超過需求；(A) 失敗，和多了 46% 的博士接不上。

stem: Which of the following may be inferred from the third paragraph?

options.A: PhD graduates in Austria are not encouraged to work outside university.
options.B: Most German PhDs work at permanent jobs immediately after graduation.
options.C: It is much easier for American PhD holders to find a teaching position than a research job.
options.D: It is more difficult for PhDs to get a permanent job five years after graduation in Slovakia than in Spain.

ev.t: Statistics show that five years after receiving their degrees, more than 60% of PhDs in Slovakia and more than 45% in Belgium, the Czech Republic, Germany, and Spain are still on temporary contracts.

note: 這一題答對率只有 51%，要把第 3 段的數字換算成選項的說法。判斷步驟：[1] 原文說取得學位五年後，斯洛伐克超過 60% 的博士仍是約聘（temporary contracts），西班牙是超過 45%；[2] 約聘的比例越高，找到長期工作的比例就越低，所以五年後在斯洛伐克比在西班牙更難找到長期工作，是 (D)。(B) 照抄 German，德國五年後仍有超過 45% 是約聘，不可能大多數一畢業就有長期工作；(A) 照抄 Austria，原文說奧地利約三分之一的博士從事和學位無關的工作，沒有說他們不受鼓勵到大學以外工作；(C) 照抄 America，原文說美國新增的教授職位只有 16,000 個，接著說研究工作的情形也差不多，兩者都難找，看不出教職比較容易。
map: five years after receiving their degrees

stem: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward the increase of PhDs in recent years?

options.A: Concerned.
options.B: Supportive.
options.C: Indifferent.
options.D: Optimistic.

note: 第 2 段說二次大戰以後各國博士人數大量增加；第 3 段一開頭就說研究人員提出警告，博士的供給遠遠超過需求，接著舉出教職太少、多年仍是約聘、從事和學位無關的工作等數字；第 4 段最後說，有些人開始懷疑念博士是不是好的選擇。作者對博士人數增加感到憂心，所以是 (A)。(B) 支持、(D) 樂觀，和第 3 段的警告與數字相反；(C) 漠不關心，作者用了兩段舉證說明供過於求的問題，並不是不在意。

stem: According to the report, how many presidential US $1 coins were scheduled to be released by the end of 2007 altogether?

options.A: One.
options.B: Two.
options.C: Three.
options.D: Four.

ev.t: The Mint will issue four presidential US $1 coins a year through 2016.
The George Washington coin is the first to be released. John Adams, Thomas Jefferson and James Madison coins will come out later this year.

note: 這一題答對率只有 55%，題目問到 2007 年底總共排定發行幾枚，要自己算。判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說這篇報導刊登在 2007 年 2 月，所以 this year 是 2007 年；[2] 第 2 段說華盛頓硬幣是第一枚，約翰·亞當斯、傑佛遜和麥迪遜的硬幣今年稍後推出，1＋3＝4；[3] 同一段也說鑄幣局每年發行四枚（four … a year），兩處算出來一樣。所以是 (D)。選 (A) 的是只算了 2 月已經發行的華盛頓硬幣，漏了 later this year 那三枚；(C) 三枚正好相反，只算了今年稍後推出的亞當斯、傑佛遜和麥迪遜，漏了 2 月已經發行的華盛頓硬幣；(B) 的「兩枚」對得上第 4 段的 He will have two!，但那是說 Cleveland 一個人會有兩枚，和 2007 年發行幾枚無關。

stem: Why did the Mint issue the US $1 coins?

options.A: In response to U.S. citizens’ requests.
options.B: In memory of the late U.S. presidents.
options.C: To attract more train commuters.
options.D: To promote the trading of dollar bills.

ev.t: The gold-colored coin is the first in a new series by the U.S. Mint to honor former U.S. presidents.

note: 第 2 段說這個新系列是美國鑄幣局為了紀念（honor）歷任美國總統推出的，第 4 段又說總統必須過世滿兩年才能上硬幣，所以選項說紀念已故的（late）美國總統，是 (B)。(D) 照抄 dollar bills，民眾用舊紙鈔兌換新硬幣，是發行當天發生的事，不是發行的目的；(C) 民眾到火車站兌換硬幣，和吸引搭火車通勤的人無關；(A) 原文沒有說是應民眾的要求發行。

stem: What may you find on the heads side of the new US $1 coin?

options.A: The name of a U.S. president.
options.B: The year when the coin was made.
options.C: The Statue of Liberty.
options.D: English proverbs.

ev.t: Each coin will show a different president on its face, or heads side. It will also show the president’s name.

note: 第 3 段說每一枚硬幣的正面（heads side）是一位不同的總統，也會刻上這位總統的名字（the president’s name），所以是 (A)。(B) 和 (C) 都照抄同一段的字，但位置不對：發行年份刻在硬幣邊緣（edge），自由女神像在另一面（The other side）；(D) 原文說邊緣刻的是傳統的標語（mottos），不是英文諺語，而且也不在正面。

stem: Which of the following can be inferred about the presidential coins?

options.A: President Gerald Ford’s coin was issued in 2008.
options.B: The U.S. Mint has issued all the presidential coins by now.
options.C: No presidential coin has been released for President Barack Obama.
options.D: Every U.S. president had his coin made two years after his term was over.

ev.t: a president cannot appear on a coin when he is still alive.

note: 第 4 段說總統在世的時候不能出現在硬幣上。考試當年（2010 年）的美國總統是歐巴馬，他還在世，所以還沒有發行他的硬幣，是 (C)。(A) 照抄 Gerald Ford，原文說福特是排在最後的一位，硬幣依任職先後每年發行四枚，從 2007 年發到 2016 年，不會在 2008 年就輪到他；(D) 照抄 two years，原文說的是總統過世滿兩年才能上硬幣，不是卸任兩年後；(B) 報導說這系列會一直發行到 2016 年，不可能已經全部發行完畢。

stem: Why did the French government decide to launch the free newspaper program?

options.A: To fight economic recession.
options.B: To win approval from youngsters.
options.C: To promote newspaper readership.
options.D: To improve the literacy rate in France.

ev.t: giving away papers to young readers in an effort to turn them into regular customers.
Newspaper readership in France has been especially low among young people.

note: 第 1 段說法國政府把報紙免費送給年輕讀者，希望把他們變成固定的訂戶（regular customers）；第 2 段接著說法國年輕人閱讀報紙的比例（readership）特別低。政府推出這個計畫，就是要提高看報的人數，所以是 (C)。(B) 討年輕人歡心，原文說的是把年輕人變成訂戶，不是爭取他們的認同；(A) 對抗經濟衰退、(D) 提高識字率，原文都沒有提到。

stem: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?

options.A: Everyone considers the government project creative.
options.B: Newspaper readership is much higher in other countries.
options.C: Research shows young people have no interest in current affairs.
options.D: Giving away free papers is not a strong enough incentive to attract readers.

ev.t: French readers, young and old, already have plenty of free options from which to choose
Some bloggers said the new program might hold the most appeal to the few young people who do already read, and buy, newspapers.

note: 第 4 段說法國讀者本來就有很多免費的選擇，網站和市中心發送的免費報紙都有；有些網誌作者也說，這個計畫最吸引的，可能是本來就會買報的少數年輕人。也就是說，免費報紙到處都是，光是免費，不足以吸引新的讀者，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 readership，原文只有法國的數字，沒有和其他國家比較；(C) 照抄 young people，原文的研究說年輕人看付費報紙的比例下降，沒有說他們對時事沒有興趣；(A) 第 3 段的 Schwartzenberg 對這個計畫有疑慮，不是每個人都覺得它有創意。

stem: What is Mr. Schwartzenberg’s attitude toward this program?

options.A: Skeptical.
options.B: Devoted.
options.C: Optimistic.
options.D: Indifferent.

note: 這一題答對率只有 39%，判斷步驟：[1] Schwartzenberg 的看法都在第 3 段，原文說他對這個計畫有很強的疑慮（strong reservations），have reservations about 是有保留、有疑慮的意思；[2] 他接著說報紙應該從讀者身上增加收益，而不是送報紙，又說這只會讓大家更相信報紙應該免費，是非常糟糕的觀念；[3] 他不相信這個計畫行得通，態度是懷疑的，所以是 (A) Skeptical。(B) 熱衷投入、(C) 樂觀，都和他的批評相反；(D) 漠不關心，他明確提出反對的理由，並不是不在意。

stem: According to the passage, where would the information about the free newspaper program in France most likely be seen?

options.A: In magazines.
options.B: On blogs.
options.C: In newspapers.
options.D: On the Internet.

ev.t: the government said the primary channel for the ads would be the Internet.

note: 第 5 段說法國政府要用廣告活動宣傳這個計畫，廣告主要的管道會是網路（the Internet），所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 4 段的 bloggers，網誌作者是對計畫發表看法的人，不是政府打廣告的管道；(C) 照抄 newspapers，計畫要推廣的是報紙，原文說宣傳的管道主要是網路，不是報紙；(A) 原文沒有提到雜誌。

stem: What does “This” in the second paragraph refer to?

options.A: Civet Coffee.
options.B: Blue Mountain coffee.
options.C: The high price of Kopi Lowak.
options.D: The unique taste of Kona.

ev.t: which sells for as much as US $50 per quarter-pound.
This isn’t particularly surprising

note: 第 2 段第一句說 This 並不令人意外，因為全世界一年只有大約 500 磅。供應量少可以解釋的是價錢貴，所以 This 指的是第 1 段最後說的麝香貓咖啡四分之一磅要價 50 美元，是 (C)。三個錯誤選項都照抄第 1 段的字：(A) Civet Coffee 是這種咖啡本身，供應少解釋的是它的價錢，不是咖啡；(B) 藍山和 (D) 可娜是拿來對照的高檔咖啡，第 2 段談的是麝香貓咖啡，而且原文也沒有提到可娜的味道。

stem: Why is Kopi Lowak expensive?

options.A: There is a very limited supply of the beans.
options.B: The coffee trees that grow the beans are scarce.
options.C: It takes a long time for the coffee beans to ripen.
options.D: Only a few experts know how to produce the beans.

ev.t: approximately 500 pounds a year of Kopi Lowak constitute the entire world supply.
In fact, it’s not the plants that are rare.

note: 這一題答對率只有 51%，(B) 是最大的陷阱。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說麝香貓咖啡貴並不意外，因為全世界一年的供應量（supply）只有大約 500 磅，所以貴是因為量少，是 (A)；[2] (B) 說咖啡樹稀少，但原文接著說 it’s not the plants that are rare，稀少的不是咖啡樹，而是麝香貓的糞便，選項說的正好是原文否定的；[3] (C) 照抄第 3 段的 ripeness，原文說椰子狸會挑最成熟的果實，沒有說咖啡豆要很久才成熟；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 experts，咖啡專家是願意花錢買咖啡的人，不是生產咖啡豆的人。

stem: What is the main point discussed in the third paragraph?

options.A: Why palm civets like the coffee beans.
options.B: Where Kopi Lowak is mainly harvested.
options.C: What chemicals are found in the civet’s digestive system.
options.D: How palm civets change coffee fruit to Kopi Lowak beans.

ev.t: A chemical substance in the digestive system of the palm civet causes some changes to the beans to give them a unique flavor.
Another possible reason is that palm civets have an unfailing instinct for picking the coffee cherries at the peak of their ripeness.

note: 第 3 段先介紹椰子狸，接著說牠們吃下整顆咖啡果實，咖啡豆在體內發生變化（changes），最後再補充另一個可能的原因：椰子狸會挑最成熟的果實。整段在說咖啡果實怎麼經過椰子狸變成麝香貓咖啡豆，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄 digestive system，原文只說消化系統裡有一種化學物質，沒有說是哪些化學物質，只講到這一段的一個細節；(A) 椰子狸愛吃咖啡果實只是一句話，這一段的重點不是牠們為什麼喜歡；(B) 原文沒有說麝香貓咖啡主要在哪裡採收，第 4 段說的是在哪裡銷售。

stem: Which of the following statements is true, according to the passage?

options.A: Little palm civets eat only the outer layer of the coffee cherries.
options.B: Palm civets somehow know the right time when the coffee fruit ripens.
options.C: Kopi Lowak is most popular in Southeast Asia and the Indonesian islands.
options.D: Kona and Blue Mountain are the most expensive coffees but only of average quality.

ev.t: palm civets have an unfailing instinct for picking the coffee cherries at the peak of their ripeness.

note: 這一題答對率只有 47%，三個錯誤選項都照抄原文的字，要逐項回原文核對。判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段最後說椰子狸天生就能準確挑出最成熟的咖啡果實，instinct 是本能，選項換成不知怎麼就是知道（somehow know）果實成熟的時機，所以是 (B)；[2] (A) 照抄 outer，原文說椰子狸把整顆果實吃下去（eat the fruit whole），只是只消化外層的果肉，選項說只吃外層，和原文不同；[3] (C) 照抄 Southeast Asia，那是椰子狸的原生地，第 4 段說麝香貓咖啡大部分在日本銷售；[4] (D) 照抄 Kona，第 1 段說可娜和藍山是高品質、價錢驚人的咖啡，最貴的是麝香貓咖啡，也沒有說它們品質普通。

stem: What caused Grass to feel confused and troubled when he was young?

options.A: He was the son of a Nazi and a victimized Pole.
options.B: He found himself fighting two opposing political parties.
options.C: He was trained to be an artist though he wanted to be a poet.
options.D: He was born with so many talents that he couldn’t choose a direction.

ev.t: His father was a German who joined the Nazi party in World War II, while his mother was Polish.
As a result, he constantly suffered contradictory feelings

note: 第 1 段說葛拉斯的父親是加入納粹黨（Nazi party）的德國人，母親是波蘭人（Polish），因此（As a result）他一直承受矛盾的感受，所以是 (A)。三個錯誤選項都照抄同一段的字：(B) 照抄 political，原文的 political activism 是他後來譴責納粹的政治行動，不是夾在兩個政黨之間；(C) 照抄 poet，原文沒有說他受訓當藝術家卻想當詩人；(D) 照抄 talents，第 1 段說他的才華展現在很多領域，這是優點，不是讓他煩惱的原因。

stem: Why has Grass been praised as “the conscience of the nation”?

options.A: He victimized the Poles and criticized the Nazis.
options.B: He has been a strong advocate of peace and justice.
options.C: He has shown great sympathy for the Poles through his poems.
options.D: He joined the Nazi party and showed great loyalty to his country.

ev.t: His commitment to the peace movement and the environmental movement as well as his unfailing quest for justice

note: 第 1 段最後說，葛拉斯投入和平運動（peace movement），始終不懈地追求正義（justice），因而贏得「國家的良心」的美譽，選項把 commitment 和 quest 換成大力倡導（a strong advocate），所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 Nazi party，加入納粹黨的是他的父親；(A) 照抄 victimized，原文說他覺得自己是受害的波蘭人，也覺得自己有傷害波蘭人的罪，並不是他真的傷害了波蘭人；(C) 照抄 Poles，原文沒有說他用詩表達對波蘭人的同情。

stem: Why was Grass’s trip to Italy important to him?

options.A: He was inspired by a fine arts master in Italy.
options.B: He formed a new interest in painting simple objects there.
options.C: He developed a new form for creating his poems during the trip.
options.D: He found a new way to solve the conflict between the Nazis and the Poles.

ev.t: he was inspired during a trip to Italy to write a poem with his watercolor brush directly on one of his paintings.
Before long, a collection of his “water poems” was born.

note: 第 2 段說葛拉斯在義大利旅行時得到靈感，用水彩筆直接把詩寫在畫上，不久就誕生了一本「水彩詩」詩集。他在這趟旅行發展出寫詩的新形式，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 inspired，原文說他得到靈感，沒有說是義大利某位藝術大師啟發了他；(B) 照抄 simple，原文說他描繪喜愛的東西，但沒有說這是在義大利開始的新興趣；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 Nazis，納粹和波蘭人的衝突是他內心的煎熬，和義大利之行無關。

stem: Which of the following correctly characterizes Grass’s poems, according to the passage?

options.A: Most of his poems depict the cruelty of the Nazis.
options.B: The theme of his poems won him the Nobel Peace Prize.
options.C: The poems on his paintings are often not related to objects in the real world.
options.D: The ideas in his poems are expressed more thoroughly with the help of his paintings.

ev.t: When he cannot find words to convey his thoughts, painting helps him find the words to express himself.

note: 第 2 段說葛拉斯找不到文字表達想法的時候，繪畫能幫他找到表達自己的字句，選項換成他詩裡的想法藉由畫作表達得更完整，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 1 段的 Nazis，原文說他譴責納粹，沒有說他大部分的詩描寫納粹的殘暴；(B) 照抄 Nobel，他得的是諾貝爾文學獎，不是和平獎；(C) 照抄 objects，原文說他描繪生活中喜愛的東西，像是甜瓜、蔬菜，詩畫的題材都來自真實世界，選項說反了。
map: with the help of his paintings

stem: Which of the following will NOT cause stress, according to the passage?

options.A: Oversleeping.
options.B: Growing up.
options.C: A busy schedule.
options.D: Living in a noisy neighborhood.

ev.t: Our environment contains such stressors as noise, crowding, time demands at home and work
These changes include the physiological changes that occur in growing into adolescence
chronic lack of sleep.

note: 題目問哪一個不會造成壓力。第 1 段提到的壓力源可以對上三個選項：(B) 長大，原文是 growing into adolescence，進入青春期的生理變化；(C) 行程很滿，原文是 time demands at home and work，家裡和工作上的時間壓力；(D) 住在吵雜的社區，原文是 noise，噪音。原文提到的是長期睡眠不足（chronic lack of sleep），沒有提到睡太多，所以是 (A)。(A) 的 Oversleeping 是睡太多，和原文的睡眠不足方向相反，不要看到 sleep 就以為原文提過。

stem: When do thought processes become a source of stress?

options.A: When we lose the ability to “self-talk.”
options.B: When we forget to push the “panic button.”
options.C: When we perceive the outside world as stressful.
options.D: When we fail to notice changes in the environment.

ev.t: How you interpret, perceive or label events going on in your environment
will determine whether these perceptions will relax you or serve as a source of stress.

note: 第 2 段說你怎麼解讀、看待（perceive）周遭發生的事情，決定了這些看法會讓你放鬆，還是成為壓力的來源（a source of stress）。也就是說，把外在世界看成充滿壓力，思考過程就會成為壓力的來源，所以是 (C)。三個錯誤選項都照抄同一段的字：(A) 照抄 self-talk，原文說的是怎麼解讀內心對話，不是失去內心對話的能力；(B) 照抄 panic button，按下警報按鈕才會有壓力，選項說忘了按，方向反了；(D) 照抄 changes，原文說大腦會解讀對環境變化的內心對話，沒有說沒注意到變化會造成壓力。

stem: What does “self-talk” refer to in this passage?

options.A: Remembering something.
options.B: Actually talking to oneself.
options.C: Responding to the environment.
options.D: Thinking about what is happening.

ev.t: Experts estimate that people can think up to 200 words per minute.
Our brain interprets the “self-talk” about changes in our environment

note: 第 2 段先說思考過程可能是壓力來源，接著說人每分鐘可以想到多達 200 個字，再說大腦會解讀對環境變化的 self-talk。從前後文看，self-talk 是腦子裡想的話，也就是對發生的事情的想法，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 talk，self-talk 加了引號，是比喻腦中的想法，不是真的開口跟自己說話；(C) 照抄 environment，回應環境是解讀之後的事，self-talk 是對環境變化的想法本身；(A) 記得某件事，和原文說的解讀、看待事情接不上。

stem: What is the best title for this passage?

options.A: How to Manage Stress
options.B: Where Does Stress Come From?
options.C: Self-talk as a Source of Stress
options.D: Stress Is Unavoidable in Modern Society

note: 第 1 段說壓力通常有三個來源：環境、身體和思考過程，接著說明環境和身體；第 2 段說明第三個來源，也就是思考過程。全文都在談壓力從哪裡來，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 self-talk，內心對話只是三個來源中的一個，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 unavoidable，壓力無法避免只是開頭第一句，過於狹隘；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 manager，原文只說怎麼回應壓力是關鍵，全文沒有教怎麼管理壓力，偏離主題。

stem: According to the passage, children like to keep chameleons or anoles as pets because ______.

options.A: they look cute
options.B: they change color
options.C: they eat insects
options.D: they have traditionally been kept as pets

ev.t: Both can change color
This is the trait that has made chameleons and anoles popular as pets.

note: 原文說兩者都會變色（change color），接著說正是這個特點（This is the trait），讓變色龍和綠變色蜥成了受歡迎的寵物，This 指的就是前一句的變色，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 insects，吃昆蟲是兩者的共同點，但原文沒有說這是受歡迎的原因；(D) 照抄 pets，原文說好幾代的美國孩子都知道變色龍這個名字，沒有說牠們受歡迎是因為向來就當寵物養；(A) 原文沒有說牠們長得可愛。

stem: The anole changes color to ______.

options.A: deceive insects
options.B: show emotion
options.C: match the background
options.D: scare off predators

ev.t: it is determined by factors such as light and temperature or by emotions such as fright, triumph, or defeat.

note: 原文說綠變色蜥變色取決於光線和溫度等因素，或是害怕、得意、挫敗等情緒（emotions），所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 background，原文用 is not, as many people think 說得很清楚，綠變色蜥變色和背景的顏色無關，這是很多人的誤解；(A) 照抄 insects，原文只說牠們吃昆蟲，沒有說變色是為了騙昆蟲；(D) 原文沒有提到嚇走天敵。

stem: What makes the chameleons and anoles different animals?

options.A: The food they eat.
options.B: Their ability to change color.
options.C: Their popularity as pets.
options.D: The number of eggs they lay.

ev.t: The chameleon lays from two to forty eggs at a time; the anole only a single egg.

note: 原文先說兩者有很多共同點，後面再列出差別：分布的地方不同，產蛋的數量也不同，變色龍一次產兩顆到四十顆蛋（eggs），綠變色蜥一次只產一顆，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 change color，原文說兩者都會變色，這是共同點，只是程度不同；(C) 照抄 pets，受歡迎是兩者都有的；(A) 兩者都主要吃昆蟲，吃的東西相同。

stem: What is a special value of anoles in the laboratory?

options.A: They lay only a single egg.
options.B: They have special hormones.
options.C: Their social behavior can be observed.
options.D: They change color less often than chameleons.

ev.t: under appropriate conditions, they will establish the same social system and behavior in the laboratory that they display in their natural environment.

note: 原文最後說，綠變色蜥作為實驗動物的特別價值，在於只要條件合適，牠們在實驗室裡會建立起和自然環境中一樣的社會體系和行為（social system and behavior），研究人員就能在實驗室裡觀察牠們的社會行為，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 single egg，一次只產一顆蛋是和變色龍的差別，不是實驗價值；(B) 照抄 hormones，原文說綠變色蜥適合研究行為和荷爾蒙的交互作用，沒有說牠們有特別的荷爾蒙；(D) 原文說綠變色蜥變色的能力比較有限，但這和實驗價值無關。

stem: According to the passage, who started the banking system?

options.A: The king of England.
options.B: Parliament members.
options.C: Goldsmiths.
options.D: London citizens.

ev.t: In exchange for their gold, the depositors received “goldsmith’s notes.”
These notes were the first bank notes.

note: 第 1 段說人們把黃金交給倫敦的金匠保管；第 2 段說存黃金的人換到「金匠票據」（goldsmith’s notes），這些票據就是最早的鈔票，後來還當作貨幣使用；第 3 段說金匠把多發的票據借給別人收利息。存款、發行鈔票、放款都是金匠開始做的，所以是 (C)。三個錯誤選項都照抄第 1 段的字：(A) 國王和 (B) 國會是內戰的雙方，人們就是怕黃金落到他們手裡才交給金匠；(D) 倫敦市民是把黃金交給金匠的人，不是經營銀行業務的人。

stem: People left their gold in the hands of the goldsmiths because the goldsmiths ______.

options.A: issued bank notes
options.B: could keep it safe
options.C: could add the value of the gold
options.D: were supported by the Parliament

ev.t: who naturally had their own methods of safe-keeping.

note: 第 1 段說人們把黃金交給金匠，因為金匠自然有他們自己的保管方法（methods of safe-keeping），選項換成金匠能把黃金保管好，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 bank notes，金匠票據是人們交出黃金以後才拿到的，是結果，不是原因；(D) 照抄 Parliament，原文說倫敦是國會的大本營，沒有說國會支持金匠，人們把黃金交給金匠，正是不想讓任何一方拿走；(C) 原文沒有說金匠能讓黃金增值。

stem: Why did people prefer to keep bank notes rather than real gold?

options.A: Bank notes were easier to carry.
options.B: Keeping bank notes was a new fashion.
options.C: Bank notes had become a legal currency.
options.D: People could earn interest from bank notes.

ev.t: they proved to be very popular with their recipients, as gold was heavy and cumbersome.

note: 第 2 段說拿到票據的人都很喜歡，因為黃金又重又不方便攜帶（heavy and cumbersome），反過來說，票據比較容易攜帶，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 currency，票據是先在收票人之間流行起來，不久才開始當作貨幣使用，原文也沒有說這時已經合法；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 interest，收利息的是借錢給別人的金匠，不是拿著票據的人；(B) 原文沒有說拿票據是一種流行。

stem: What is most likely the reason for the founding of the Bank of England?

options.A: To increase the national income.
options.B: To lend gold to London citizens.
options.C: To stop the practice of using gold as currency.
options.D: To prevent goldsmiths from making illegal profits.

ev.t: they began to issue more notes than the gold they had.
This practice was questioned but never tested in court.
this practice of creating money out of thin air was effectively made legal with the founding of the Bank of England.

note: 原文沒有直接寫英格蘭銀行為什麼成立，要從第 3 段推。判斷步驟：[1] 金匠發行比手上黃金還多的票據，再把這些錢借出去收利息，這種做法有人質疑，合不合法一直沒有定論；[2] 1694 年英格蘭銀行成立以後，憑空創造金錢的做法才合法化，等於把這種做法納入正式成立的銀行，不再是金匠私下賺取有疑慮的利潤；[3] 四個選項中，只有 (D) 防止金匠賺取不法利潤和這個脈絡相合。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 London，銀行借出去的是新創造出來的錢，不是黃金；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 currency，票據本來就以黃金作擔保，原文沒有說要停止用黃金當貨幣；(A) 原文沒有提到國家收入。

stem: Which of the following has puzzled Mayan scholars?

options.A: Why Mayan cities disappeared.
options.B: Why Mayan culture ceased to exist.

options.D: Why Mayan civilization was not shaped by one single country.

ev.t: One question that interests scholars is why these cities just disappeared.

note: 第 2 段說學者感興趣的一個問題，是這些城市為什麼就這樣消失了（why these cities just disappeared），後面又說學者對當時發生了什麼事情看法不一，可見這個問題讓學者困惑，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄 ceased，原文說的是城市不再是重要的中心，馬雅文化延續了下來，至今仍然存在，選項說文化消失，和原文相反；(D) 照抄 one single，馬雅文明不是統一的帝國，這是原文直接說明的事實，不是學者困惑的問題；(C) 原文沒有討論馬雅文化為什麼沒有傳出中美洲。

stem: Which of the following is considered a factor in the disappearance of Mayan city-states?

options.A: Dense population.
options.B: Spread of the tropical jungle.
options.C: Invasion by other civilizations.
options.D: Overprotection of the environment.

ev.t: Another factor considered is overpopulation.
the Mayan population reached up to 200 people per square kilometer

note: 第 3 段說另一個納入考量的因素是人口過多（overpopulation），馬雅的人口密度最高達到每平方公里 200 人，選項換成人口稠密（Dense population），所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 tropical jungles，城市淹沒在叢林裡是消失以後的事，不是原因，第 4 段反而說熱帶森林幾乎沒有剩下；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 environment，原文說的是破壞環境（destruction），選項的過度保護說反了；(C) 原文說的是城邦之間互相攻打，不是其他文明入侵。

stem: According to the passage, what was the consequence of overuse of the tropical forest?

options.B: Overpopulation.
options.C: Continuous wars.

ev.t: Overpopulation led to overuse of the tropical forest, the source of their food.
Research from pollen indicates that there was almost no tropical forest left.

note: 第 3 段說人口過多導致熱帶森林過度利用，而森林是他們糧食的來源（the source of their food）；第 4 段說熱帶森林幾乎沒有剩下。糧食的來源用光了，結果就是糧食短缺，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 overpopulation，人口過多是森林過度利用的原因，不是結果，選項把因果倒過來了；(C) 照抄 wars，城邦之間的戰爭是另一個因素，原文沒有說是森林過度利用造成的；(A) 第 4 段說的是缺水和乾旱，和洪水相反。

note: 第 1 段介紹馬雅文明的成就和鼎盛時期；第 2 段提出問題：古典期以後，這些城市為什麼消失了；第 3、4 段說明戰爭、人口過多、資源過度利用和環境破壞等因素。全文的重點在馬雅城市的衰亡，所以是 (A)。(B) 馬雅文明的興起只在第 1 段，過於狹隘；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 Classic Period，古典期的發展也只在第 1 段，過於狹隘；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 tropical jungles，叢林只是淹沒了消失的城市，文章不是在談叢林和馬雅文明的關係，偏離主題。

stem: The purpose for having a Take Our Daughters to Work Day is ______.

options.B: to let girls spend more time with their mothers
options.C: to show girls possibilities for work and careers

ev.t: to expose girls to expanding opportunities for women in the workplace.
The program offers millions of girls a first-hand view of the many career opportunities available in their futures.

note: 第 1 段說這個活動的目的，是讓女孩看到女性在職場上越來越多的機會（opportunities）；第 2 段接著說，活動讓女孩親眼看到未來可以選擇的各種職業（career opportunities），選項把 opportunities 換成 possibilities，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 top，原文說數學、科學通往薪水最高的工作，是在說明男女的差距，活動的目標是給女孩信心和啟發，不是鼓勵她們追求高薪；(B) 和 (D) 看活動名稱「帶女兒上班」就猜和媽媽有關，但原文沒有提到陪媽媽或參觀媽媽的辦公室。

stem: TOD was criticized because some people ______.

options.B: did not like having children at work

ev.t: TOD had been criticized for excluding boys

stem: Which of the following is true according to the passage?

options.A: Boys are now included on Take Our Daughters to Work Day.
options.B: Women and men have always been treated equally at work.
options.C: Homemaking and rearing children are jobs for girls only.
options.D: Girls grow up receiving more attention than boys.

ev.t: it was expanded in 2003 to include boys.

note: 第 4 段說 TOD 在 2003 年擴大，把男孩也納入（include boys），所以是 (A)。(B) 第 3 段說女性的平均薪資只有男性的 73%，高階主管和科技領域的女性也遠遠偏少，職場上的男女一直沒有得到平等的對待；(C) 第 4 段引用 Gould 的話，說應該讓男孩知道當托育人員也是可以接受的選擇，照顧小孩不是只有女孩能做；(D) 第 3 段說男孩在課堂上得到比較多的鼓勵，選項說反了。

stem: Why are women underrepresented in some fields such as technology?

options.A: They are not interested in these fields.
options.B: They are not encouraged to work in these fields.
options.C: They are not paid the same as men in these fields.
options.D: They are not allowed to be educated in these fields.

ev.t: At school, boys often receive more encouragement in the classroom, especially in math, science and computer science

note: 這一題答對率只有 46%，原文沒有用 because 直接說原因，要把第 3 段前後幾句連起來。判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段說女性在高階主管職位和科技領域的人數遠遠偏少（underrepresented）；[2] 同一段前面說，在學校，男孩在數學、科學和電腦科學這些學科得到比較多的鼓勵（encouragement），而這些學科正是通往科技領域的路；[3] 反過來說，女孩在這些學科沒有得到同樣的鼓勵，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄 paid，女性薪資比較低是同一段的另一個事實，原文沒有說這是她們很少進入科技領域的原因；(A) 原文沒有說女性對這些領域沒興趣；(D) 原文說的是鼓勵比較少，不是不准受教育。

stem: The topic of this passage could best be described as ______.

options.A: the scientific study of hairstyles
options.B: the symbolic meanings of hairstyles
options.C: the art of designing different hairstyles
options.D: the contemporary development of hairstyles

note: 第 1 段說古埃及的假髮代表身分和地位；第 2 段說凱爾特人和參孫的長髮代表力量；第 3 段說古希臘的捲髮代表生活態度；第 4 段說龐克和 1960 年代女性用頭髮表達反抗。全文談的是頭髮在不同時代象徵什麼，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 artistry，假髮做工講究只是古埃及的一個細節，過於狹隘；(D) 當代的髮型只在第 4 段，過於狹隘；(A) 文章沒有談髮型的科學研究，偏離主題。

stem: Why did ancient Greeks like to wear curls and locks?

options.A: To attract others.
options.B: To show off their artistry.
options.C: To hide their real identity.
options.D: To represent power and status.

ev.t: The ancient Greek word for curls and locks is related to intriguing and tempting someone.

note: 這一題答對率只有 39%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段先說捲髮象徵改變、自由和生活的樂趣，這三個說法選項都沒有用；[2] 最後一句說古希臘文的捲髮這個字，和引起別人興趣、誘惑別人（tempting someone）有關，也就是吸引別人；[3] 選項換成 attract others，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 1 段的 artistry，做工講究說的是古埃及的假髮；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 status，代表身分地位的也是古埃及人的外表，代表力量的是第 2 段的長髮，都不是古希臘的捲髮；(C) 原文沒有說捲髮是為了隱藏身分。

stem: How did women in the 1960s use hair to show objection?

options.A: They grew long hair.
options.B: They dyed their hair.
options.C: They cut their hair short.
options.D: They shaved their heads.

ev.t: Women’s liberation was expressed in a short-cut, straight and simple hairstyle

note: 第 4 段說 1960 年代的女性解放運動，透過剪短（short-cut）、直順、簡單的髮型來表達，選項換成她們把頭髮剪短，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 2 段的 long hair，留長髮的是凱爾特人，而且長髮在女人身上代表生育能力，不是反抗；(B) 把頭髮染成嚇人顏色的是今天的龐克運動；(D) 原文沒有提到剃光頭。

note: 這一題答對率只有 49%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說參孫的力量來自他的長髮，唯一知道這個祕密（secret）的人是大利拉；[2] 大利拉替敵人當間諜，出賣他，剪掉了他的頭髮；[3] 如果參孫沒有把祕密告訴任何人，就沒有人知道要剪他的頭髮，他可能就不會落敗，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 curly hair，捲髮是古典希臘時期的流行，1960 年代流行的是直順的短髮，選項的 always 說法太過武斷；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 Egypt，原文說古埃及人很重視外表，假髮做工講究，選項說反了；(C) 照抄第 4 段的 punk，原文沒有說龐克運動是歷史上最成功的運動之一。

stem: What’s the writer’s purpose of writing this passage?

options.A: To recommend youth service programs to schools.

options.D: To propose alternatives for doing community services.

note: 第 1、2 段舉了三個孩子當志工的例子；第 3 段說全世界每年有數百萬個孩子幫助社區；第 4 段說不景氣時社區服務特別重要；第 5 段說當志工的孩子長大後更可能繼續做好事，最後直接對讀者說：拿起油漆刷、垃圾袋，幫助你的社區吧。全文是在鼓勵孩子參加志工活動，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 youth service，學校提供服務活動只是第 3 段的內容，作者並不是在向學校推薦，過於狹隘；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 charitable organizations，原文說的是孩子幫慈善機構補上缺口，不是要求慈善機構服務社區，偏離主題；(D) 文章沒有提出社區服務的替代方案，偏離主題。

stem: What is the main idea of the 3rd paragraph?

options.A: Community service is gaining popularity among children.
options.B: Families and schools help to make community service popular.
options.C: Children now depend more on their teachers than on their parents.
options.D: Nathan White had a special reason to raise money for medical research.

ev.t: Schools and parents also contribute to the rise in youth service.

note: 第 3 段的第二句是主題句：學校和家長也促成了青少年服務的增加（contribute to the rise），接著用 For example 說學校怎麼做，再用 on the other hand 說家長怎麼做。選項把 schools and parents 換成 families and schools，把 contribute to the rise 換成 help to make … popular，所以是 (B)。(A) 孩子越來越熱衷社區服務，只是這一段的開頭，接下來的內容都在說學校和家長的角色；(C) 照抄 teachers，原文說老師和家長都在鼓勵孩子，沒有比較孩子比較依賴誰；(D) 照抄第 2 段的 Nathan White，那是第 2 段的例子。

stem: Why is community service important in a time of recession?

options.A: It raises money for school activities.

ev.t: many charitable organizations have experienced a significant drop in donations.
Camille and other children who volunteer thousands of hours annually can fill in some of the gaps.

options.D: Children who do volunteer work are more likely to grow up to be caring adults.

stem: Why is it common for students to download copyrighted music?

options.A: They don’t think that they will be caught.
options.B: They want their friends to know that they are smart.
options.C: They think it is a good way to make some extra money.
options.D: They are against copyright protection over Internet music.

ev.t: I always thought the threat was just a scare tactic.
“You know, everyone does it,” added Mike.

note: 第 3 段 Mike 說，他一直以為那些警告只是嚇唬人的手段，又說大家都在下載；Sandra 也說，直到主管機關跟她聯絡，她才知道下載是違法的。他們都沒想到自己會出事，也就是認為自己不會讓人抓到，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄 money，Mike 說的是想省點錢（save some money），不是賺外快；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 copyright，原文沒有說學生反對網路音樂的版權保護；(B) 原文沒有說學生下載是要讓朋友覺得自己聰明。

stem: What does Mike mean by saying that “the threat was just a scare tactic”?

options.A: One should not be afraid of threats.
options.B: A lawsuit will result from the threat.
options.C: It is unfair to scare people with a threat.
options.D: No serious consequence will follow the threat.

ev.t: I always thought the threat was just a scare tactic.
Mike expressed shock and couldn’t believe that this was happening to him.

note: 這一題答對率只有 55%，判斷步驟：[1] scare tactic 是嚇唬人的手段，just a scare tactic 是說這些警告只是嚇唬人，不會真的怎麼樣；[2] 前一句說 Mike 非常震驚，不敢相信這種事會發生在自己身上，可見他原本以為警告之後不會有嚴重的後果；[3] 所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 lawsuit，Mike 後來確實吃上官司，但這是他沒料到的事，不是他說這句話的意思；(A) 不應該害怕威脅、(C) 用威脅嚇人不公平，都是在評論威脅，Mike 說的是他以為威脅不會成真。

stem: What is RIAA’s attitude towards students’ illegal downloading behavior?

options.C: A Survey of Students’ Downloading Habits
options.D: Eliminate Illegal Music Download? Impossible!

note: 第 1 段說未經許可下載有版權的音樂就是違法；第 2 段說學生非法下載很普遍，最後一句說這些做法是要付出代價的；第 3 段舉出 Sandra 繳罰款、Mike 付錢和解的例子；第 4 段說 RIAA 認為沒有後果，學生就不會改變。全文在警告侵犯版權的人要小心後果，所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄第 2 段的 survey，學生下載習慣的調查只是第 2 段的內容，過於狹隘；(B) 文章不是在教讀者怎麼取得免費音樂，偏離主題；(D) 照抄第 4 段的 illegal，原文說光靠教育不夠，要有後果才能改變行為，並沒有說非法下載不可能杜絕，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following is true about the name Lego?

options.A: It is a combination of Greek and Latin words.
options.B: It was created by Ole Kirk Christiansen’s son.
options.C: It was created in 1947 for naming the plastic toys.
options.D: It came from Danish words meaning “play” and “well.”

ev.t: putting together the first two letters of the Danish words Leg and Godt, which mean “play well.”

note: 第 1 段說 Lego 這個名字，是把丹麥文（Danish words）Leg 和 Godt 兩個字的前兩個字母拼起來，意思是「好好玩」（play well），所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 Greek，原文說這個名字也可以用拉丁文、希臘文解釋，但名字是從丹麥文來的，不是希臘文和拉丁文組成的；(B) 照抄第 2 段的 son，取名字的是 Ole Kirk Christiansen 本人，兒子是後來改良積木的人；(C) 照抄第 2 段的 1947，那是開始做塑膠玩具的年份，名字是 1932 年的兩年後就有了。

stem: When did the Lego brick become as a creative form of toy?

ev.t: saw the immense potential in Lego bricks to become a system for creative play.
In 1958, the modern interlocking brick design was finally developed and patented.

note: 這一題答對率只有 51%，四個選項都是原文出現過（或算得出來）的年份，要分清楚每個年份發生了什麼事。判斷步驟：[1] 1932 年 Christiansen 開始做木頭玩具，兩年後（1934 年）想到 Lego 這個名字；[2] 1947 年開始做塑膠玩具，但賣不好，很多貨都退了回來；[3] 兒子看出積木可以發展成激發創意的遊戲系統（a system for creative play），花了好幾年改進積木互扣的能力，1958 年互扣式積木終於研發完成，積木到這時才成為激發創意的玩具。所以是 (A)。(B) 1947 和 (D) 1932 照抄原文的年份，但那時還沒有互扣的積木；(C) 1934 是取名字的年份。

stem: Which of the following is true in describing the popularity of Lego?

options.A: More than 5 billion people in the world own Lego sets.
options.B: Children spend an average of 62 dollars on Lego bricks each year.
options.C: People in the world spend 400 million hours playing with Lego every year.
options.D: The Lego Group now produces more than 30 thousand toy bricks every minute.

ev.t: Every minute 33,824 Lego bricks are made

note: 第 3 段說每分鐘生產 33,824 塊樂高積木，選項換成每分鐘生產超過三萬塊，所以是 (D)。三個錯誤選項都照抄同一段的數字，但把數字接到別的事情上：(A) 50 億是全世界的孩子一年玩樂高的小時數，不是擁有樂高的人數；(B) 62 是平均每個人擁有的積木塊數，不是花多少錢；(C) 4 億是今年玩樂高的人數，不是小時數。

stem: What is most likely the reason why Lego still remains popular?

options.A: Old Lego bricks may still be connected to new ones.
options.B: The company hasn’t changed its name since 1947.
options.C: The material for the bricks has proved to be safe.
options.D: The price of the toy is relatively reasonable.

ev.t: Bricks bought then are still compatible with current bricks and that is probably the reason the toy has never fallen out of favor.

note: 第 4 段說當年買的積木，仍然可以和現在的積木組在一起（compatible with current bricks），這大概就是樂高從來沒有退流行的原因，選項換成舊積木仍然可以和新積木接在一起，所以是 (A)。(B) 照抄第 2 段的 1947，那是開始做塑膠玩具的年份，原文說的是產品五十年沒變，不是名字沒變；(C) 材料安全、(D) 價格合理，原文都沒有提到。

stem: What is “anorexia nervosa” as mentioned in the first paragraph?

options.A: It is an inability to express one’s feelings.
options.B: It describes a situation of feeling insecure.
options.C: It refers to people who are emotionally unstable.
options.D: It is an illness that makes one want to stop eating.

ev.t: It was not enough to be thin. I had to be the thinnest.
a helpless childlike emotion that came from starving.

note: anorexia nervosa 是神經性厭食症。就算不認得這個詞，也可以從前後文推出來：第 1 段接著說光是瘦還不夠，一定要最瘦，又說父親說她胖以後就開始節食；第 2 段說她專注在挨餓（starving）帶來的虛弱感；第 3 段說她康復以後重了三十八磅。這是一種讓人不想吃東西的病，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 express，不善於表達感情的是她的父親；(B) 照抄第 3 段的 secure，原文說她現在覺得很安心，選項的 insecure 拿這個字反過來用，不是厭食症的意思；(C) 情緒不穩定的人，和她挨餓、節食的描述接不上。

stem: Why did the writer suffer from anorexia nervosa?

options.A: She was told by her father to take care of herself.
options.B: She wanted to go to the best university.
options.C: She wanted her father’s attention.
options.D: She grew up in a poor family.

ev.t: I liked to know that I needed to be taken care of; maybe Daddy would take care of me.
By starving, I attempted to gain pride in myself by obtaining my father’s approval or acknowledgment of my value as a person.

note: 第 2 段說她喜歡知道自己需要別人照顧，也許爸爸就會來照顧她；第 3 段說她用挨餓的方式，想得到父親的認可（approval）和肯定。她生病是想得到父親的注意，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 take care of，是她希望爸爸來照顧她，不是父親叫她照顧自己；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 best universities，那是父親對她的期待，她自己說從來不覺得有討好父親的壓力，原文也沒有說她生病是因為想念最好的大學；(D) 原文沒有提到家境貧窮。

stem: Which of the following statements is true about the writer?

options.A: She has problems controlling her tempers.
options.B: She is proud of herself for working hard to succeed.
options.C: She has had great confidence in herself since childhood.
options.D: She has changed her father’s way of expressing himself.

ev.t: I know that I am a valuable person who strives to achieve and accomplish.

note: 這一題答對率只有 32%，正確選項的說法和原文差最多，要對照第 3 段整段來看。判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段說她知道自己是有價值的人，會努力追求成就（strives to achieve and accomplish），strive 是努力，achieve、accomplish 是成功，選項換成 working hard to succeed；[2] 同一段最後說，最重要的認可必須來自自己，現在她覺得很安心，也就是她為努力上進的自己感到驕傲；[3] 所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄 express，原文說她無法改變父親不善於表達感情，選項說反了；(C) 她九年級時想靠父親的認可肯定自己，到康復以後才學會接納自己，不是從小就有自信；(A) 原文沒有提到她控制不住脾氣。

stem: What’s the writer’s purpose of writing this passage?

options.A: To blame her father.
options.B: To report a case of child abuse.
options.C: To reflect on a stage of growing up.
options.D: To teach people how to lose weight.

note: 第 1 段作者說她九年級時得了厭食症，現在完全康復，回頭省思（reflect back），明白病因和她跟父親的關係有關；第 2 段回顧她當時的心情；第 3 段說她學會接納自己，最重要的認可要來自自己。全文是作者回顧、省思自己成長中的一個階段，所以是 (C)。(A) 作者說她無法改變父親，只能接納自己，並沒有怪罪父親，偏離主題；(B) 原文沒有提到虐待兒童，偏離主題；(D) 作者寫的是從厭食症康復的經過，不是教人減肥，偏離主題。

stem: What happened to the territorial lines drawn in Africa by the Europeans?

options.A: They disappeared as the Europeans no longer ruled the colonies.
options.B: They were respected by different ethnic groups.
options.C: They became borders between countries.
options.D: They became war memorials.

ev.t: When the colonies became independent nations, these same borderlines were often maintained.

note: 這一題答對率只有 43%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說歐洲人劃分殖民地時畫了邊界（borderlines）；[2] 第 2 段第一句說，殖民地成為獨立的國家（independent nations）以後，往往沿用（maintained）原來的邊界；[3] 也就是說，殖民時期的邊界成了國與國之間的邊界，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 Europeans，歐洲人不再統治以後，邊界並沒有消失，反而沿用下來，選項說反了；(B) 第 3 段說這些邊界拆散族群、引發衝突，族群並沒有尊重這些邊界；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 war，邊界引發了戰爭，但沒有變成戰爭紀念碑。

stem: What does the author think to be a reason for conflicts among the Africans?

options.A: Most ethnic groups have established their own countries.
options.B: One ethnic group is broken up among different countries.
options.C: Some Europeans invaded Africa to increase their colonies.
options.D: African nations fought the Europeans to expand their territories.

ev.t: the Somali people remain split among Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Djibouti.
a war between Somalia and Ethiopia was fought because Somalis wanted all their people to be a part of one nation.

note: 這一題答對率只有 45%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段第一句說衝突的起因，是同一個族群拆散到不同的地方、又和別的族群劃在一起；[2] 接著舉例：索馬利人分散在衣索比亞、肯亞、索馬利亞和吉布地四國（第 2 段的 split），他們希望所有同胞屬於同一個國家，因此和衣索比亞打了一場戰爭；[3] 選項把 split 換成 broken up，說一個族群分散在不同的國家，所以是 (B)。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 colonies，原文說歐洲人劃分殖民地時沒有考慮族群，但衝突發生在非洲國家之間或國內族群之間，不是歐洲人為了擴大殖民地入侵；(D) 照抄第 1 段的 territories，原文的 territories 是各族群的領域，沒有說非洲國家和歐洲人打仗擴張領土；(A) 原文說幾乎每一個非洲國家都住著不只一個族群，和大多數族群都有自己的國家相反。

stem: What is the best title for the passage?

options.A: War and Peace in Africa
options.B: Africa: Borderlines Misplaced
options.C: European Colonization of Africa
options.D: Africa Recovered and Reconstructed

note: 這一題答對率只有 42%，三段都圍繞同一件事：第 1 段說歐洲人劃殖民地時，邊界沒有考慮族群；第 2 段說獨立以後沿用這些邊界，族群分散各國，也有很多族群劃在同一國；第 3 段說因此引發衝突。全文的重點是非洲的邊界劃錯了地方，misplaced 就是放錯位置，所以是 (B)。(A) 照抄第 3 段的 peace，非洲的戰爭與和平範圍太大，文章只談邊界造成的族群衝突，太過廣泛；(C) 照抄第 1 段的 colonies，歐洲人劃分殖民地只是第 1 段的背景，過於狹隘；(D) 文章沒有談非洲的復原和重建，偏離主題。

stem: Why did Andrew Carnegie move to the United States?

options.A: Because his father was offered a good job in Pittsburgh.
options.B: Because he did not want to follow his father’s profession.
options.C: Because there were serious political problems in Scotland.
options.D: Because his family could not make a good living in their hometown.

ev.t: But the industrial revolution destroyed the weavers’ craft, and the family had to leave for new possibilities in America.

note: 這一題答對率只有 54%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說卡內基家是織布工，工業革命摧毀了織布工的手藝（destroyed the weavers’ craft）；[2] 家裡賴以為生的行業沒了，在家鄉就難以維持生計，所以全家只好到美國找新的機會；[3] 選項換成在家鄉無法好好過活，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 father’s profession，原文說大家期待他繼承父親的行業，沒有說他不想，搬家是因為這個行業沒落了；(A) 照抄第 2 段的 Pittsburgh，原文說的是到美國尋找新的機會，沒有說父親在匹茲堡找到好工作；(C) 照抄 Scotland，原文說的是工業革命，不是政治問題。

stem: When did Carnegie begin to show his interest in artistic and intellectual pursuit?

options.A: After he retired from his business.
options.B: When he was a young boy back in Scotland.
options.C: After he earned his fortune from his iron business.
options.D: When he worked as a messenger boy in Pittsburgh.

ev.t: later worked as a messenger boy in the telegraph office.
He was often asked to deliver messages to the city theater, where he would stay to watch plays by great playwrights.
He also spent most of his leisure hours in a small library

note: 這一題答對率只有 37%，最多人選的陷阱是 (A)。判斷步驟：[1] 題目問他什麼時候「開始」展現對藝術和求知的興趣；[2] 第 2 段說他在匹茲堡當送信童（messenger boy）的時候，常常把電報送到劇院，送完就留下來看大劇作家的戲（藝術），空閒時間大多待在圖書館（求知），所以是 (D)；[3] (A) 照抄第 4 段的 retire，原文說強烈的求知慾讓他賣掉公司退休，求知慾是退休的原因，早在退休以前就有了，不是退休以後才開始。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 fortune，賺大錢是在南北戰爭以後，比當送信童晚得多；(B) 照抄 Scotland，原文只說他在蘇格蘭時大家期待他繼承父親的行業，沒有提到他的興趣。

stem: Which of the following best characterizes how Carnegie managed his business?

options.A: He was willing to make new changes.
options.B: He set out to beat all the other competitors.
options.C: He was happy to make more money in the shortest time.
options.D: He did not hesitate in making investments in his hometown.

ev.t: He devoted himself to the replacement of wooden bridges with stronger iron ones and earned a fortune.
He further introduced a new steel refining process to convert iron into steel.

note: 這一題答對率只有 44%，題目問的是怎麼經營事業，要從第 3 段他做了哪些事去推。判斷步驟：[1] 他用更堅固的鐵橋取代木橋（replacement），又引進新的煉鋼方法（introduced a new … process），把鐵煉成鋼；[2] 取代舊的、引進新的，都是願意做新的改變；[3] 所以是 (A)。(C) 照抄第 4 段的 make more money in the shortest time，原文說他對滿腦子想著用最短時間賺更多錢感到不安，怕自己墮落，選項說他樂在其中，方向相反；(B) 原文沒有說他要打敗其他競爭對手，只說他的產量超過全英國；(D) 他投資的是美國的鋼鐵業，原文沒有提到在家鄉蘇格蘭投資。

trap.t: make more money in the shortest time

stem: How did Carnegie handle his fortune after his retirement?

options.A: He left it to his family and friends after he died.
options.B: He gave it to poor people and charity organizations.
options.C: He used it to support organizations of higher learning.
options.D: He invested it in developing new technology in steel refinement.

ev.t: He abhorred charity; instead, he used his money to help others help themselves. He established over 2,500 public libraries, and sponsored numerous cultural, educational and scientific institutions.

note: 這一題答對率只有 35%，最多人選的陷阱是 (B)。判斷步驟：[1] 第 5 段說他憎惡施捨（abhorred charity），abhor 是憎惡的意思，所以他不是把錢直接施捨給窮人和慈善機構，(B) 照抄 charity，意思正好相反；[2] 原文接著用 instead 說他用錢幫助別人自助：設立超過 2,500 座公共圖書館，資助無數文化、教育和科學機構（institutions）；[3] 選項把教育和科學機構換成高等學術機構（organizations of higher learning），所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 died，原文說他過世時已經捐出 3 億 5,000 萬美元，沒有說留給家人朋友；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 steel refining，那是他經營事業時引進的煉鋼方法，退休後他已經賣掉公司。

stem: What is the cause of AD/HD?

options.A: Gene problem.
options.B: Academic pressure.
options.C: Illness in childhood.
options.D: Inappropriate home environment.

ev.t: AD/HD is a neurological disorder which stems not from the home environment, but from biological and genetic causes.

note: 第 2 段說注意力不足過動症的原因不在家庭環境，而在生理和遺傳（genetic causes），選項把 genetic 換成 gene，所以是 (A)。(D) 照抄 home environment，原文用 not … but … 說得很清楚，原因不是家庭環境，選項說反了；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 academic，學業表現出問題是症狀造成的結果，不是原因；(C) 照抄 childhood，原文說症狀通常在幼年時期出現，是說出現的時間，不是說幼年生病造成的。

stem: Which of the following are most likely AD/HD patients?

options.A: Children who are very lazy.
options.B: Children who are very attentive.
options.C: Children who act over-cautiously.
options.D: Children who have learning difficulties.

ev.t: Depression, anxiety, and learning disabilities may co-exist with AD/HD.

note: 這一題答對率只有 53%，題目問 most likely，要找原文和選項最接近的一句。判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段說學習障礙（learning disabilities）可能和注意力不足過動症同時存在；[2] 第 1 段也說，有這種疾患的孩子學業表現會出問題，第 2 段說他們很難專心學習新的東西；[3] 有學習困難的孩子最可能是患者，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄 attentive，原文說的是 inattentive（注意力不足），選項的 very attentive 說反了；(C) 過度小心，和原文說的衝動、不經思考相反；(A) 原文沒有說患者很懶，過動的孩子反而總是靜不下來。

stem: What is the first thing to do if your child is suspected of AD/HD?

options.A: Report it to the school.
options.B: Consult a professional.
options.C: Wait until the child grows up.
options.D: Send the child to a special school.

ev.t: if a child is suspected of AD/HD, it is very important that he or she be evaluated by a professional.

note: 這一題答對率只有 43%，最多人選的陷阱是 (A)，要分清楚兩件事的先後。判斷步驟：[1] 題目問的是懷疑（suspected）孩子有這種疾患時，第一件事做什麼；[2] 第 3 段說，如果懷疑孩子有注意力不足過動症，請專業人員（a professional）評估非常重要，選項換成諮詢專業人員，所以是 (B)；[3] (A) 照抄第 4 段的 school，原文說的是孩子一旦確診（Once your child is diagnosed）以後，才要讓學校知道，那是評估之後的事。(C) 等孩子長大，原文沒有這樣說；(D) 原文說學校會在課堂上做調整，沒有說要送孩子去特殊學校。

stem: Why are diamonds from some areas called “blood diamonds”?

options.A: They resemble blood in color.
options.B: They cause loss of human lives.
options.C: They represent love and passion.
options.D: They are of exceptionally high quality.

ev.t: They are places where citizens have been terrorized or even killed by groups in control of the local diamond trade.

note: 第 1 段說販賣衝突鑽石的錢用來資助叛軍和恐怖組織，在這些國家，控制鑽石交易的團體恐嚇人民，甚至殺害（killed）人民。這些鑽石造成人命損失，所以叫血鑽石，是 (B)。(A) 血鑽石的「血」是比喻流血和死亡，原文沒有說鑽石的顏色像血；(C) 愛情和熱情，是一般人對鑽石的印象，和原文說的恐嚇、殺害無關；(D) 原文沒有提到鑽石的品質。

stem: What can be inferred from the second paragraph of this passage?

options.A: Diamonds from Liberia are mostly conflict-free.
options.B: Most diamonds from Liberia are labeled correctly.
options.C: Diamonds in Liberia are still traded to support wars.
options.D: Diamonds from Liberia have been carefully investigated by the KPCS.

ev.t: the problem of conflict diamonds hasn’t gone away.
Diamonds mined in some rebel-held areas, such as Liberia, are being smuggled into neighboring countries and exported as conflict-free diamonds.

note: 這一題答對率只有 36%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段第一句說，戰爭大多已經結束或減緩，但衝突鑽石的問題並沒有消失；[2] 接著說賴比瑞亞等叛軍控制的地區，開採出來的鑽石走私到鄰國，再當作無衝突的鑽石出口；[3] 叛軍控制的地區還在賣鑽石，可見賴比瑞亞的鑽石仍然在交易，用來支持戰爭，所以是 (C)。(A) 照抄 conflict-free，原文說這些鑽石是「當作」無衝突的鑽石出口，實際上是衝突鑽石，選項把偽裝當成事實；(B) 鑽石走私出境、冒充無衝突的鑽石，標示並不正確；(D) 照抄第 3 段的 KPCS，題目問的是第 2 段，而且原文沒有說 KPCS 仔細調查過賴比瑞亞的鑽石。

stem: What is the major task of the KPCS?

options.A: To promote the sales of rough diamonds.
options.B: To produce movies like Blood Diamond.
options.C: To penalize those who sell blood diamonds.
options.D: To document where the diamonds were mined.

ev.t: The goals of the KPCS are to document and track all rough diamonds when they enter a participating country.
provide enough detailed information about their origins to prove they did not originate in a conflict zone.

note: 這一題答對率只有 41%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 3 段說 KPCS 的目標，是在原鑽進入參與國時記錄（document）並追蹤；[2] 運貨的人要提供詳細的產地資料（origins），證明鑽石不是來自衝突地區；[3] 記錄並證明產地，就是選項的記錄鑽石是在哪裡開採的，所以是 (D)。(A) 照抄 rough diamonds，KPCS 追蹤原鑽是為了阻止血鑽石交易，不是推銷原鑽；(B) 照抄第 4 段的 Blood Diamond，那是 2006 年的電影，和 KPCS 無關；(C) 原文只說要記錄、追蹤、提供產地證明，沒有提到懲罰賣血鑽石的人。

stem: What is the author’s attitude towards blood diamonds?

options.A: Indifferent.
options.B: Threatening.
options.C: Sympathetic.
options.D: Disapproving.

note: 這一題答對率只有 29%，最多人選的陷阱是 (C)，要分清楚態度的對象。判斷步驟：[1] 題目問的是作者對血鑽石（blood diamonds）的態度；[2] 第 1 段說販賣血鑽石的錢用來資助不法活動，控制當地鑽石買賣的團體恐嚇、殺害人民；第 3 段說南部非洲國家想辦法阻止血鑽石交易；第 4 段呼籲讀者多了解衝突鑽石造成的問題，買鑽石時憑良心做選擇。作者不贊成血鑽石，所以是 (D) Disapproving；[3] (C) Sympathetic 是同情，作者同情的是第 4 段受動亂和苦難折磨的人民，不是血鑽石本身。(A) 漠不關心，和作者呼籲讀者了解問題不符；(B) 作者是在提醒讀者，沒有威脅誰。

stem: This passage is most likely taken from a ______.

options.A: cookbook
options.B: user’s manual
options.C: consumer report
options.D: fashion magazine

note: 第 1 段從便利商店的商品包裝說起；第 2 段說明日本人為什麼用比較多的包裝、包裝市場的規模、新包裝推出的速度，以及產品要怎麼滿足消費者的需求。全文是從消費的角度分析商品包裝，最可能出自消費報導，所以是 (C)。(A) 食譜、(B) 使用手冊，文章沒有教人怎麼做菜或怎麼使用產品，偏離主題；(D) 時尚雜誌談的是穿著打扮，文章談的是商品包裝，偏離主題。

stem: Which of the following is NOT a reason for the Japanese to use more packaging?

options.A: Packaging helps to keep food fresh.
options.B: Packaging helps the Japanese to show appreciation.
options.C: The Japanese consider packaging a symbol of quality.
options.D: Packaging is a way to compete with Westerners in economy.

ev.t: a cultural emphasis on freshness
they believe nice packaging adds value because it’s a strong signal of quality.
the Japanese are more connected with packaging as a symbol of appreciation, love and care.

note: 這一題答對率只有 51%，題目問哪一個不是日本人多用包裝的原因，要逐項回第 2 段核對。判斷步驟：[1] (A) 對上 a cultural emphasis on freshness，文化上重視新鮮；[2] (C) 對上 a strong signal of quality，包裝是品質的訊號；[3] (B) 對上 a symbol of appreciation，包裝象徵感謝。剩下 (D)：原文的 compared with Westerners 是說日本人比西方人更重視包裝的象徵意義，是一個比較，並沒有說日本人用包裝在經濟上和西方人競爭，所以是 (D)。(D) 拿原文出現過的 Westerners 和 economy 拼在一起，看起來像原文提過。

stem: The word “shelf-mates” in the second paragraph most likely refers to ______.

options.A: co-workers on the job
options.B: other products in the store
options.C: customers’ need for other products
options.D: other graphic designs on the package

ev.t: a product has to have more than just a nice graphic design to differentiate it from its shelf-mates.

note: 這一題答對率只有 31%，shelf-mates 是作者自己組合的字，要拆開來看。判斷步驟：[1] shelf 是貨架，mate 是同伴，像 classmate 是同班的人，shelf-mate 就是擺在同一個貨架上的東西；[2] 這一句說一項產品（a product）要和它的 shelf-mates 區別開來，能拿來和產品比較、擺在同一個貨架上的，是店裡的其他產品；[3] 所以是 (B)。(D) 照抄同一句的 graphic design，平面設計是用來區別產品的方法，不是拿來比較的對象；(C) 照抄後一句的 needs，消費者的需求不會擺在貨架上；(A) mate 有同事的意思，但這裡和 shelf 組合，說的是貨架上的商品，不是工作上的同事。

stem: The white man tried to kill the gray wolf because ______.

options.A: it attacked people
options.B: it damaged the crops
options.C: it was adored by the Indians
options.D: it threatened the life of his livestock

ev.t: Western ranchers continued to claim that thousands of cattle were killed every year by wolves.

note: 這一題答對率只有 42%，關鍵是 livestock 這個字。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說西部的牧場主人宣稱，狼每年咬死好幾千頭牛（cattle）；[2] livestock 是家畜、牲口，牛就是牧場主人的家畜；[3] 選項換成狼威脅到家畜的生命，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 1 段的 Indians，印第安人敬重狼，但原文沒有說白人是因為這樣才殺狼；(A) 原文說狼咬死的是牛，沒有說狼攻擊人；(B) 原文沒有提到農作物。

stem: This passage was most likely written by someone who ______.

options.A: liked hunting wild animals
options.B: made laws against the gray wolf
options.C: advocated the protection of the gray wolf
options.D: appreciated the gray wolf’s hunting skills

ev.t: The last wolves in the American West died hard.
The vast lands of the American West fell silent. The country had lost its greatest predator.

note: 作者沒有直接表明身分，要從用字推。第 2 段把殺狼稱為戰爭（war），第 3 段說最後的狼死得很慘，連國家公園都不安全；第 4 段說西部的土地陷入一片寂靜，這個國家失去了它最偉大的掠食者（its greatest predator）。作者對狼的消失感到惋惜，最可能是主張保護灰狼的人，所以是 (C)。(D) 照抄第 1 段的 hunting skills，敬佩狼的狩獵本領的是印第安人，作者是在介紹他們的看法；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 hunt，作者對殺狼感到惋惜，不像喜歡打獵的人；(B) 立法對付灰狼的是國會和蒙大拿，作者的語氣是惋惜，不是站在他們那一邊。

stem: What was an important reason for the fast disappearance of the wolf?

options.A: The wolf could not have the cattle as food.
options.B: The Indians killed the wolves for their skins.
options.C: National park rangers killed most of the wolves.
options.D: The government encouraged the killing of wolves.

ev.t: In 1884, Montana created its first wolf bounty
Moreover, the government even provided free poison.
ranchers persuaded the United States Congress to provide funds to exterminate wolves on public lands.

note: 這一題答對率只有 49%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段說蒙大拿祭出懸賞，殺一隻狼賞一美元，後來提高到八美元；[2] 政府還免費提供毒藥，國會也撥款在公有土地上消滅狼；[3] 懸賞、毒藥、撥款都是政府在鼓勵殺狼，所以是 (D)。(C) 照抄第 3 段的 park rangers，黃石公園的巡山員殺了將近 140 隻狼，但蒙大拿三十五年間領賞的狼屍超過八萬具，巡山員殺的不是大多數；(A) 照抄 cattle，原文說的是狼吃牛，不是狼吃不到牛；(B) 照抄第 1 段的 skins，印第安人披狼皮是為了得到狼的本領，原文沒有說他們為了狼皮殺狼。

stem: The Indians respected the wolf because it ______.

options.A: was good at hunting
options.B: was good at disguising
options.C: had beautiful skins and paws
options.D: was an enemy to the white man

ev.t: They respected the animals’ endurance and hunting ability

note: 這一題答對率只有 50%，三個錯誤選項都照抄第 1 段的字，要分清楚原因和做法。判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說印第安人敬佩（respected）狼的耐力和狩獵能力（hunting ability），選項換成狼很會狩獵，所以是 (A)；[2] (B) 照抄 disguises，偽裝是印第安人披上狼皮去突襲，是人在偽裝，不是狼擅長偽裝；[3] (C) 照抄 skins and paws，他們披狼皮狼爪，是希望得到狼的狩獵本領，不是因為狼皮漂亮；[4] (D) 照抄 white man，原文說印第安人不理解白人對狼的戰爭，沒有說狼是白人的敵人，所以敬重牠。

stem: What is the author’s attitude toward abortion?

options.A: For it.
options.B: Against it.
options.C: Neutral.
options.D: Indifferent.

note: 這一題答對率只有 28%，作者的立場要看用字和最後一段。判斷步驟：[1] 第 2 段作者稱超音波是美好的科技（blessed technology），說醫師的熱情讓人耳目一新；[2] 第 4、5 段引述支持墮胎的人的批評，用的是 hostile（敵意）、aghast（驚駭）這類字眼，作者站在他們的對面；[3] 第 6 段直接表態：生命權優先於女性的選擇權，沒有什麼比胎兒的笑臉更有說服力。作者反對墮胎，所以是 (B) Against it。(A) 支持墮胎，是第 4、5 段受訪者的立場，不是作者的；(C) 中立，作者在最後一段明確表態，並不中立；(D) 漠不關心，作者用整篇文章論述，不是不在意。

stem: How have the pro-abortionists reacted to the photos of smiling unborn babies?

options.A: All with disbelief and scorn.
options.B: All with applause and appreciation.
options.C: Some with respect and some with scorn.
options.D: Some with applause and some with disappointment.

ev.t: says the photos are simply misleading, and ridicules the anti-abortion lobby
the pro-abortion lobby is having the same hostile reaction.

note: 這一題答對率只有 18%，選項的 All 和 Some 是關鍵。判斷步驟：[1] 第 4 段的 Anne Carp 說照片根本是在誤導（misleading），等於不相信照片（disbelief），還嘲笑（ridicules）反墮胎團體，嘲笑就是 scorn；Geoff Brodie 也抱怨這些照片會讓反墮胎團體利用；[2] 第 5 段說美國支持墮胎的團體也有同樣的敵意（the same hostile reaction）；[3] 原文引述的支持墮胎的人，反應全都是不信和嘲笑，沒有一個例外，所以是 (A)。(C) 和 (D) 用 Some 把反應分成兩種，原文沒有任何一位支持墮胎的人表示尊重或讚賞；(B) 第 2 段說喜歡這些照片的是準爸媽，不是支持墮胎的人。

stem: Which of the following people is most likely an anti-abortionist?

options.A: Anne Carp.
options.B: Geoff Brodie.
options.C: Stuart Campbell.
options.D: A writer for the American Prospect.

ev.t: His outspoken enthusiasm for this blessed technology is refreshing.
I hear so many couples laughing when they see the pictures—it’s wonderful.

note: 這一題答對率只有 24%，要先把文章裡的人分成兩邊。判斷步驟：[1] 第 4、5 段的 Anne Carp、Geoff Brodie 和《美國展望》的作者，都在批評這些照片，第 3 段已經點明他們是支持墮胎的運動人士，(A)、(B)、(D) 排除；[2] 公布照片的 Stuart Campbell 醫師，對這項科技充滿熱情，說爸媽都很喜歡，看到照片都笑了；[3] 作者稱讚他的熱情讓人耳目一新，而作者本身反對墮胎；在四個人當中，Campbell 最可能是反對墮胎的人，所以是 (C)。原文沒有直接說 Campbell 反對墮胎，這是從他的態度和作者的立場推出來的。

stem: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: It is wrong for doctors to publish pictures of unborn babies.

options.D: Anti-abortionists are pleased with the ultrasound photos of unborn babies.

ev.t: ridicules the anti-abortion lobby for being “intoxicated with evidence of a fetus’ humanity.”
will be picked up by those groups that use anything and everything to stop abortions

note: 這一題答對率只有 28%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 4 段 Anne Carp 嘲笑反墮胎團體「陶醉於胎兒具有人性的證據」，可見反墮胎團體把這些照片當成證據，看了很高興；[2] Geoff Brodie 也說這些照片會讓不擇手段阻止墮胎的團體拿去利用；[3] 反墮胎的人樂見這些超音波照片，所以是 (D)。(B) 照抄第 5 段的 fetus，反墮胎的人正是認為胎兒具有人性，和新生兒一樣是生命，選項說反了；(A) 照抄第 1 段的 published，原文沒有說醫生公布胎兒照片是錯的，作者還稱讚這位醫師；(C) 第 6 段作者主張生命權優先於選擇權，可見並不是每個人都同意女性可以自己決定。

stem: According to the passage, how tall will the Dubai Tower be?

options.A: At least 43 stories higher than Toronto’s CN Tower.
options.B: 180 feet higher than Toronto’s CN Tower.
options.C: At least 22 stories higher than the Taipei 101.
options.D: 160 feet higher than the Taipei 101.

ev.t: The current tallest, at 101 floors, is the Taipei 101 in Taiwan
visitors will swoon over this city from 123 stories high, if not more.

note: 這一題答對率只有 50%，要算一下樓層數。判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說目前最高的台北 101 有 101 層；[2] 杜拜塔完工後是 123 層，甚至更高（if not more）；[3] 123 減 101 是 22，再加上 if not more，杜拜塔至少比台北 101 高 22 層，所以是 (C)。(B) 照抄 180 feet，那是 CN Tower 比台北 101 高出的高度；(D) 照抄 160 feet，那是杜拜塔地基樁深入地下的深度，不是比台北 101 高出多少；(A) 照抄第 3 段的 43，那是大金字塔稱霸的世紀數，不是樓層數。

stem: The main purpose for building the Dubai Tower is ______.

It’s image, clearly

note: 這一題答對率只有 30%，判斷步驟：[1] 第 1 段說 Boll 的科學成就讓他的人生停擺，良心不安，美夢成了惡夢；[2] 第 2 段最後說，Amai 看穿 Boll 的外表，開始體會他為了勝利付出的代價（the price he has paid for victory）；[3] 打贏戰爭的一方也付出了代價，作者要說的是戰爭的勝利一定要付出代價，所以是 (D)。(B) 過於狹隘，只講第 1 段 Boll 每年演講替自己辯護，他的良心其實一直不安；(A) 偏離主題，Boll 正是希望藉著 Amai 替自己贖罪；(C) 偏離主題，Boll 為了曼哈頓計畫的成功受盡折磨，並不引以為傲。
